RWAMAGANA, Rwanda – The Rwandan government has begun testing a centralised school meal system that prepares food in large quantities and delivers it to schools – a mechanism similar to ones operating in Japan and South Korea.

The shift, says education ministry, is also aimed at reducing reliance on firewood, improving nutrition and lowering the cost of school feeding.

The pilot launched Friday serves 15,014 students and 266 teachers across five public schools in Rwamagana District.

Meals are prepared at a central kitchen and transported to the schools in electric vehicles, replacing the need for each institution to cook its own food.

The facility, located at GS Bujyujyu in Muyumbu Sector, was inaugurated on Friday, November 13, by the Minister of State for Education, Claudette Irere, alongside representatives of Solid’Africa, the local social enterprise implementing the project.

The arrangement follows a hub-and-spoke model also used in Japan, where municipal school lunch centres, known as kyushoku centres , prepare meals for distribution to several schools.

Japan has developed this system alongside school-based kitchens as part of a nationwide school feeding programme.

The model allows large quantities of food to be prepared in specialised facilities before being transported to schools.

It also supports centralised nutritional planning and hygiene management. In Japan, school meals are considered part of education, with students often serving food to classmates and eating together in their classrooms.

South Korea also has a nationwide school meal system, although its arrangements are not identical to Japan’s. Its schools generally retain responsibility for meal operations, while procurement and distribution systems can involve centralised institutions.

Rwanda’s pilot adapts some of these principles to local conditions. Its five participating schools are GS Bujyujyu, GS Muyumbu, GS Muyumbu B, GS Murama and GS Gitagara.

Speaking at the inauguration, Irere said access to nutritious meals was directly linked to children’s ability to learn and perform well in school.

“Every child in Rwanda deserves a good education, and no child should have to sit through a lesson on an empty stomach,” she said.

“Hunger makes learning harder. As we work to improve what children learn in school, we must also ensure they have the nourishment they need to make the most of every school day.”

She thanked Solid’Africa, The Rockefeller Foundation and other partners for supporting investments in school feeding infrastructure.

One of the main differences between Rwanda’s approach and older centralised school kitchen systems elsewhere is its emphasis on clean energy.

The facility operates within a one-hour delivery radius of the five schools. It prepares meals and dispatches them in electric vehicles to ensure they reach students in time for lunch.

Its energy system combines rooftop solar panels with electricity from the national grid. Industrial electric cooking equipment replaces traditional wood-burning stoves.

The arrangement is expected to eliminate harmful smoke from cooking facilities and reduce energy costs per meal. It also supports Rwanda’s target of phasing out biomass cooking in public institutions by 2030.

Centralising food preparation could also reduce the duplication of kitchens, cooking equipment, staffing and storage facilities across individual schools. However, the pilot’s assessment will determine the actual savings.

The project also connects school feeding with local agricultural production.

The kitchen purchases fresh produce from agricultural cooperatives representing approximately 1,000 smallholder farmers in the surrounding region.

Structured purchasing agreements are intended to give farmers a reliable market for their harvests. The arrangement also provides schools with locally grown ingredients.

This is another distinction in Rwanda’s approach. Rather than relying solely on large commercial suppliers, the project is designed to link public food procurement directly to smallholder farmers and rural communities.

School gardens form another part of the programme. They supplement food supplies while giving students practical lessons in nutrition and food production.

Japan’s Shokuiku , or food and nutrition education, similarly treats school meals as an opportunity to teach children about healthy diets, food production and the value of local ingredients.

The Rwamagana project follows a partnership agreement signed between the Government of Rwanda and Solid’Africa in November 2023.

Solid’Africa previously developed centralised clean-cooking systems for public hospitals in Kigali, and other referral regional hospitals.

The school kitchen extends that approach to the education sector.

Supported by catalytic funding from The Rockefeller Foundation, the facility will serve as a testing ground for the model.

Unlike Japan and South Korea, which have operated nationwide school feeding systems for decades, Rwanda is starting with a limited pilot.

The Rwamagana facility serves 15,014 students and 266 teachers, providing an opportunity to assess the model before expanding it.

Government officials and technical partners will monitor its performance over the coming school terms. The assessment will cover energy efficiency, meal delivery logistics and the cost of preparing each meal.

The findings will inform decisions on whether to establish additional regional kitchen hubs across Rwanda.

Mauricio Pochettino was emotional during his USA news conference

Mauricio Pochettino says the decision to leave his role as boss of the USA national team to become Manchester United head coach was "one of the most difficult" of his career.

The Argentine was announced as Michael Carrick's successor at Old Trafford on Friday, with sources telling BBC Sport he has signed a two-and-a-half-year contract.

United paid a release clause in the region of £7.4m to extract Pochettino from his USA contract, with a further payment being made for his backroom staff.

Pochettino only signed a new four-year deal with the USA in the summer, but will depart for Manchester after leading the national team in matches against Haiti on 14 and 18 November.

The 54-year-old broke down in tears during his first news conference after his move to United was confirmed, and thanked the US Soccer Federation for its support.

"It's difficult to talk now," he said. "I'm a very emotional guy. It's a very sad decision.

"But we are professionals and we are trying to make our dreams come true."

Asked why he signed a new deal with the national side only to accept United's offer, Pochettino said the chance to manage at Old Trafford was too good to reject.

"I never said I wanted to go back but they know there aren't too many opportunities that happen in your career like Manchester United," he said. "When it arrives, it's difficult to turn down."

Carrick was sacked on Thursday after United's worst start to a domestic campaign in 40 years, which has left them languishing in 18th place in the Premier League.

Pochettino will inherit a side that have won just once in 10 league matches this season and sit just one point above bottom-placed Sunderland.

His first match in charge will be an away match against Liverpool on 22 November.

How Ferguson-inspired Pochettino can succeed where Carrick failed at Man Utd

Pochettino's arrival at Old Trafford marks the end of a decade-long courtship.

Thriving during an 18-month stint at Southampton, he led the Saints to eighth place during his only full season on the south coast.

Tottenham moved quickly to appoint one of the most promising young coaches in Europe in 2014, and it was in north London that his reputation rocketed.

The club had finished in the top four just twice in the 22 years before his appointment, but Pochettino led them there four times in his five full seasons.

It was two years into his time in the capital that United first considered a move for Pochettino.

The Argentine dined with legendary former United boss Sir Alex Ferguson in Mayfair, London just weeks before Louis van Gaal was sacked as Red Devils boss.

The club ultimately decided to appoint Jose Mourinho, and Pochettino was again overlooked when the Portuguese departed in 2018, with Ole Gunnar Solskjaer impressing so much in an interim role that he was given the job more permanently.

In 2022, it was between Pochettino and Erik ten Hag for the United job but the board opted for the Dutchman, who had led Ajax to the semi-finals of the Champions League in 2019, when they were beaten by Pochettino's Tottenham.

Pochettino was interviewed by United again in 2024 following his exit from Chelsea, but the board opted instead to hire Ruben Amorim from Sporting to replace Ten Hag.

Pochettino in tears at USA news conference before Man Utd move

Pochettino a decade in Man Utd's making - but Carrick deserves better

Shortly after Pochettino's appointment, Carrick released a statement on social media thanking United's fans for their support during his time in charge of the club.

"Dear United fans, I've had the immense privilege of leading Manchester United, the football club that I love," wrote Carrick. , external

"There are very few who get to live that and feel it, and for that I'm incredibly grateful.

"With that comes huge responsibility, and to be at Manchester United, you need to understand exactly what that means.

In a wide-ranging post, Carrick, who signed a two-year deal with the club in May, said the club's culture and values drove him at Old Trafford.

"Ultimately, you need to push to be the best, but there is a culture, there are values and there are behaviours that you have to live by and respect, which have been built over a long period of time," he wrote.

"It's a football club that is unique, with substance and history that cannot be ignored.

"This is what inspired me every single day."

Man Utd fans give their thoughts on Mauricio Pochettino

The chaos that took Carrick from two-year deal to sacked within 15 games

Manchester United have made it pretty clear Mauricio Pochettino is the only coach they spoke to directly about taking over at Old Trafford.

Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte were also mentioned as possibles in the aftermath of that awful 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth three weeks ago, but evidently Pochettino emerged as the first choice.

Interestingly, United have felt it necessary to state privately any claim of a split between the Glazer family and Sir Jim Ratcliffe is "categorically false" in their words.

I reported earlier this week a mechanism by which the Glazer family could take back control of the football operation from Ratcliffe.

There has been no Stock Exchange statement that has happened - there was one that Ratcliffe had been handed control by the board when he agreed to buy into United in December 2023.

There has been huge criticism by fans of the way United are being run. Sporting director Jason Wilcox is blamed by many for bad recruitment, but the budget was set higher up.

United officials are keen to stress unanimity in the hierarchy but with the club 18th in the Premier League and having sacked three managers in three seasons, none of the owners can be happy. It is one to keep an eye on.

International Organisation of La Francophonie (OIF) Secretary-General Louise Mushikiwabo has praised Cambodia for its commitment and hospitality as it hosts the 20th Francophonie Summit in Phnom Penh.

Speaking at the opening of the Francophonie Village on Friday, Mushikiwabo invited the Francophone community to take part in its activities and gatherings.

She said the summit is not only a political event but also a chance for people to share experiences and build closer connections.

The summit, scheduled for November 15 and 16, will also decide who leads the OIF for the 2027–2030 term.

Four candidates are in the running: Mushikiwabo, the incumbent; Coumba Ba of Mauritania; Dacian Cioloș of Romania; and Juliana Lumumba of the Democratic Republic of Congo.

The leaders of member states are due to make their choice on November 16.

The Francophonie Village is part of the events surrounding the summit, offering a public space for activities and encounters among members of the French-speaking community.

MN202611_168tyb3murx.t:
The crash took place on a highway bordering Kaziranga National Park in the Golaghat district of Assam

At least 24 people have died and 11 others injured after a bus collided with a truck in Assam, north-east India.

The accident happened near Kaziranga National Park, a Unesco World Heritage site, and the injured have been admitted to Jorhat Medical College and Hospital.

Several of the deceased are college students, according to Assam's rural development minister Atul Bora, but they have not yet been publicly identified.

Bora added that witnesses reported one of the vehicles may have been speeding when the crash took place, but "the exact reason will be known after [an investigation]".

Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma wrote in a post on X that "the scale of this loss has shaken all of us".

He adds: "Our foremost priority now is to make sure the injured receive the best possible medical care without delay."

Family members of one of the victims pictured at the accident site

The bus was carrying passengers from Bokakhat and was headed towards Nagaon.

Bokakhat is best known as the gateway to Kaziranga National Park, famous for its one-horned rhinoceroses.

Nagaon is an important agricultural and commercial centre in central Assam, about 120km (74.5 miles) west of Bokakhat by road.

Lurinjyoti Gogoi, chief of a regional opposition party, said road safety has long been a major concern in the state.

"The government must take it up seriously," he said.

Road accidents are responsible for thousands of deaths in India every year.

In 2023, 172,000 people lost their lives on Indian roads, or 474 a day – roughly one every three minutes.

The count increased to 183,382 deaths in 2025.

Experts say the crisis is rooted not just in infrastructure but in human behaviour, enforcement gaps and systemic neglect.

Police officers involved in United Nations peace operations have discussed challenges facing deployed contingents and ways to respond to emerging security threats in their mission areas.

The discussions took place during a week-long workshop for coordinators of Formed Police Units (FPUs), held at Rwanda National Police headquarters in Kacyiru.

Participants shared experiences and explored strategies for addressing operational difficulties encountered during missions.

The workshop also covered certification related to the Assessment for Mission Service (AMS) and the Assessment of Capabilities, including training for instructors.

Rwanda’s Inspector General of Police, Commissioner General Felix Namuhoranye, and United Nations Police Adviser Police Commissioner Faisal Shahkar officially closed the workshop.

MN202611_zggpsh6q27.t:
Michael Carrick yandikiye abafana ba Manchester United ibaruwa yuzuye amarangamutima, abasobanurira agaciro gakomeye yagize ko gutoza ikipe yakunze kuva kera, anabashimira urukundo n'ubwitange bamugaragarije mu bihe byiza n'ibikomeye. Ni ibaruwa yashyize hanze nyuma y'uko ikipe ya Manchester United yatangaje ko Umunya-Argentine Mauricio Pochettino ari we mutoza mushya w'iyi kipe, asinya amasezerano azageza muri Kamena 2029.

Muri iyi baruwa, Carrick yavuze ko gutoza Manchester United ari amahirwe adasanzwe abantu bake babona, kuko ari ikipe ifite amateka, indangagaciro n'umuco wihariye bituma itandukana n'izindi.

Yavuze ko gutoza iyi kipe bijyana n'inshingano zikomeye, kuko uyibereye umutoza cyangwa umuyobozi agomba kumva neza amateka yayo, kubaha indangagaciro zayo no guharanira ko ikomeza kuba imwe mu makipe akomeye ku Isi.

Yagize ati: "Nagize amahirwe akomeye yo gutoza Manchester United, ikipe y'umupira w'amaguru nkunda. Ni abantu bake bagira amahirwe yo kubaho muri ubwo buzima no kubyumva, kandi ndabishimira cyane."

Carrick yashimangiye ko ikimushimisha kurusha ibindi ari amateka n'umuco by'iyi kipe byubatswe mu gihe kirekire, bikaba bigomba kubahwa n'umuntu wese uyibamo.

Yashimiye abafana ku rukundo bamugaragarije

Mu butumwa bwe, Carrick yashimiye by'umwihariko abafana ba Manchester United, avuga ko ari abantu badasanzwe kandi batandukanye n'abandi.

Yavuze ko bagiranye ibihe byiza n'ibikomeye, ariko ko ikimushimishije cyane ari ukubona ibyishimo n'amarangamutima bagaragazaga nyuma y'imikino, ku buryo bahitaga bifuza kongera kugaruka kuri Stade.

Yavuze ko yifuzaga kubaha ibyishimo no kubasubiza ku rukundo bamugaragarije

Nubwo yemeye ko ikipe itari imaze iminsi ibona umusaruro mwiza, yashimye abafana kuba barakomeje kumuba hafi no kumugaragariza urukundo mu gihe abandi bashoboraga guhindukira bakigendera.

Yagize ati: "Ndabizi ko tutabonye umusaruro mwiza mu mikino iheruka, ariko mwangaragarije urukundo n'inkunga mu gihe ikintu cyoroshye abantu benshi bakora ari ukugutera umugongo bakigendera. Ibyo bifite agaciro kurusha gutsinda umukino umwe cyangwa ibiri."

Carrick kandi yashimiye abari bagize itsinda rye ry'abatoza, avuga ko bamuhaye ubufasha bwose yari akeneye buri munsi, anashimira ubudahemuka, umurava n'ubufatanye bamugaragarije.

Ntiyibagiwe n'abakozi bakora inyuma y'ibikorwa bigaragara bya Manchester United, avuga ko nubwo akazi kabo kadakunze kugaragara mu ruhame, gafite uruhare rukomeye mu mikorere y'iyi kipe.

Ku bakinnyi, yabashimiye imbaraga n'ibihe byiza bagiranye, anabifuriza kuzagira amahirwe n'umusaruro mwiza mu bihe biri imbere.

Yavuze ko urukundo afitiye Manchester united rutazigera rushira

Mu gusoza ibaruwa ye, Carrick yavuze ko yifuza kubona Manchester United ikomeza gutsinda no kugera ku ntsinzi, kuko ari ikipe yagize uruhare rukomeye mu buzima bwe kandi ko ibyo bitazigera bihinduka.

Yavuze ko azahora yishimira uruhare yagize muri iyi kipe, ndetse ko n'ubwo atazaba akiyitoza, azakomeza kuyishyigikira nk'umufana. Yasoje avuga ko azakomeza kuba hafi y'iyi kipe, ayishyigikira kandi yifuriza abakinnyi bayo gutsinda.

The ship, which was once the fastest in the world and longer than the Titanic, was intentionally sunk off the coast of Florida, in order to create the world's largest artificial ocean reef.

The SS United States spent nearly 30 years docked in Philadelphia before it was moved to Florida, where it will become a home for sea life and an underwater attraction for marine enthusiasts.

Activists unsuccessfully fought for the historic liner - which crossed the Atlantic Ocean hundreds of times - to be preserved as a museum.

MN202611_y7voljol2d.t:
How could the Nvidia CEO’s affair threaten US national security?

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has blamed Howard Lutnick's Commerce Department for failing to properly oversee the export of high-spec AI chips, as the fallout from the Nvidia scandal widens to President Donald Trump's cabinet.

Pressure is building on Lutnick from across the political spectrum to explain his department's actions.

Jensen Huang was ousted as Nvidia CEO after revelations he had an affair with a businesswoman who was also allegedly a Chinese spy.

Megaspeed, the firm she worked for, had been probed by US government agencies over suspicions it was smuggling Nvidia chips into China, reports said, but was not on a list of firms US companies are prevented from working with.

Bessent told CNBC several agencies "were in favour of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months".

"But Commerce has the pen... and you will have to ask them about their internal process," he added.

Bessent's comments come after Lutnick was called to testify before the Senate Banking Committee next month over the Commerce Department's role in allowing Nvidia to export its advanced chips.

Other congressional committees have asked both Lutnick and his department to retain all records relating to Nvidia and Huang.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said some parts of the administration wanted more controls on trade with Megaspeed

Bessent said he was "frustrated" by delays in putting the company on the export control list and reports of leakage of AI chips into China.

"President Trump made it very clear that China should not receive any Nvidia chips above H100s, so any leakage is very frustrating because it hurts our great companies in the AI race, because it gives the Chinese an advantage," he said.

Last year, the Commerce Department had been investigating Megaspeed over suspicions it had been smuggling some of Nvidia's advanced AI chips into China, according to the New York Times. Megaspeed has been contacted for comment.

There was also pressure on the Commerce Department to add it to the list, but the Financial Times separately reported that the department was delaying efforts to have the cloud computing firm included.

However, Bessent also pointed the finger at Nvidia.

"The story has been thus far of Jensen Huang's personal foibles," he told CNBC , external .

"The real story here should be: did Nvidia know their client, and was there a robust effort at Nvidia to make sure that there was no leakage and that they were selling to what were obviously pass-through shell companies?

"It's important that anyone at the company there be held accountable for that."

Bessent's pointed comments are a rare instance of internal debate within the Trump administration spilling out into the public view, although tensions have reportedly simmered between Bessent and Lutnick in the past.

In 2024, the two reportedly jostled for the role of treasury secretary ahead of Trump's return to the White House, and last year the pair butted heads over the administration's tariff policy, according to US media.

How a sex scandal at Nvidia is putting pressure on the White House

How AI visionary Jensen Huang was undone by his own bad decisions

Huang has been summoned to testify before the Senate Banking Committee about his alleged affair with the former Megaspeed executive, who is suspected of being a Chinese spy.

The commerce secretary has also been summoned to appear before the committee in December.

"Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive US technology," committee chairman Republican Senator Tim Scott posted on X.

Democrats on key congressional committees have asked the Commerce Department and Lutnick to keep all records relating to decisions to allow Nvidia to sell its advanced AI chips to Chinese companies, including all their communications with or about Nvidia and Huang.

Ways and Means Committee Ranking Member Richard E Neal and Senate Finance Committee Ranking Member Ron Wyden are starting investigations into the way Nvidia was allowed to sell these chips.

They say Nvidia's advanced H200 chips could be sold to Chinese firms if they were first imported from their manufacturing facility in Taiwan into the US for inspection.

A 25% tariff - a levy paid by US importers to the federal government - was imposed on those chips under a section of the Trade Act that Neal and Wyden say is meant to allow the US president to take action against imports that risk national security.

"Trump's use of the statute appears to have done the opposite, undermining US national security and putting Americans at risk," they said.

Dorset was hit by widespread flooding earlier this year

School children are taking part in an event aimed at inspiring climate action, to coincide with the COP31 international climate conference in Turkey.

Hosted at the Kingston Maurwood campus, the first Dorset-wide Youth COP has brought children from 14 schools together to discuss issues including future careers.

Maria Clarke, of Dorset Local Nature Partnership, said young people should be "given a voice" over dealing with climate change.

A Dorset COP 2026 event is also being held on Saturday as world leaders and delegates gather at Antalya in Turkey for the COP31 climate summit.

The Dorset Youth COP event includes discussions about how young people feel about climate change as well as a panel session introducing them to the range of jobs and careers in the climate and energy sectors.

Maria Clarke, of Dorset Local Nature Partnership, said: "Young people are inheriting the climate and ecological emergencies that previous generations have created and need to be given a voice in jointly developing and implementing the solutions to these issues."

"The Youth COP aims to raise awareness, inspire and support them to take action now and into the future."

The main Dorset COP 2026 event takes place on Saturday also at the Kingston Maurward Campus near Dorchester.

The fourth annual event brings together community groups, environmental organisations, experts and political leaders.

The programme will explore how Dorset can respond to climate change, nature loss, food resilience, pollution and other environmental challenges.

The programme will also feature an exhibition of over 30 local organisations and a Question Time-style panel bringing together Dorset MPs, council leaders and independent climate experts.

Giles Watts, chair of Dorset CAN said the event's focus was on making "a lasting positive impact" on climate and nature local areas.

"We want to bring people together, listen to different perspectives and energise local communities and politicians to act more quickly on the pressing challenges we face," he added.

MN202611_3nd7ce63t8.t:
Owain Wyn Evans cycled almost 400 miles from Glasgow to Cardiff

Presenter Owain Wyn Evans has completed his challenge of cycling through all four UK nations to raise money for BBC Children in Need.

The Welsh host of BBC Radio 2's Early Breakfast Show rode almost 400 miles , setting off from Glasgow and finishing in Cardiff on Friday.

The challenge started on 9 November in Scotland and over the next five days, Owain rode through Northern Ireland, England and Wales and raised £4,760,086 in the process.

Reflecting on his journey, he said: "This has been the hardest challenge of my life, 100%.

"I can't believe I'm here. It's overwhelming, all the love and passion and commitment people have shown."

In total, Children in Need raised £38.7 million in its 46th campaign .

The BBC said Owain's challenge would be the "greatest-ever distance" covered in a Radio 2 endeavour for the charity.

He crossed the finish line in Cardiff's Central Square just after 11:00 GMT, and was greeted by a crowd cheering him on before he was met by his husband, Arran Rees.

Owain, 42, whose bike was named Shania Chain, and decked out in Children in Need colours - Pudsey's favourite yellow with coloured spots - said: "Thank you so much everyone, from me and Shania.

"Honestly, this has felt so far away for such a long time. I can't believe that I'm here with this welcome and the sun's out."

Hollywood actor Luke Evans announced the route to Owain each day on BBC Radio 2.

During the 640km feat, he was also surprised with the premiere of Steps' brand-new version of their debut hit 5, 6, 7, 8, retitled 5, 6, 7, donate, which featured new lyrics and extra vocals.

It was recorded to help boost Owain's spirits on the longest day of his challenge.

The Welsh host rode through Northern Ireland, England and Wales

When the challenge was announced, Owain, who is originally from Ammanford, Carmarthenshire, said: "I'm ready to give it absolutely everything I've got."

He said colleagues Sara Cox, Paddy McGuinness and Vernon Kay had previously achieved "extraordinary things" for Children in Need so he had "a lot to live up to".

Owain was undertaking his second challenge for the BBC charity fundraiser, following his 24-hour drumathon in 2021 , external .

The Welsh presenter was met by his husband, Arran Rees, and his parents as he completed his four-nation cycle

During the ride Owain received a heartwarming message of support from his primary school teacher Cath Adams.

Speaking to his parents on Radio 2, he recalled having a pink Care Bears lunch box while in reception because he loved the programme.

He said some classmates laughed at him and it prompted his "first feeling of shame", so he hid his lunchbox.

He added: "I remember Cath Adams bringing it out and telling the other kids that this is alright.

"And she was probably my first ally. And I never realised at the time but I love you Cath Adams, you're amazing."

Owain Wyn Evans started his four-nation cycle in Glasgow

Owain said he "is not a cyclist or an endurance athlete in any way, shape or form" but when he was asked to do this, "of course I said yes"

Pop group Remember Monday surprised Owain during his pit-stop in Shrewsbury with an acapella medley of Britney Spears hits

Owain managed a spot of drumming during his almost 400 mile cycle ride

After cycling through Scotland, Northern Ireland, England and Wales, Owain said bringing the challenge to a close in Cardiff will be "special"

Hundreds of people turned out in Cardiff to support Owain as he completed the 640km feat

Owain crossed the finish line just after 11:00 on Friday

Asked how he was feeling, Owain said: "There are so many children who need our help and who will be helped by all the donations."

Speaking to Kay, he spoke about the gruelling nature of the challenge.

"You train so hard, me and Shania Chain going around the streets, but the reality of it, it's so hard.

"It's been amazing every step of the way and that's been super emotional as well."

Owain previously admitted he "never enjoyed exercise at school" because of bullying, ahead of his four nations biking challenge.

A right royal surprise! "Well done on what you're doing, I am sending all my best wishes to you"

The broadcaster also expressed his gratitude for the support of Radio 2 listeners.

His messages of support from public figures included one from the Princess of Wales, who recorded a message for him in Welsh, saying: "Hi Owain, it's Catherine, you're doing so well. Keep going. Wishing you all the very best."

Shania Twain was so impressed that the bike had been named after her that she sent a message of good luck before the challenge.

She said: "Hi Owain, Shania Twain here. You're about to take on an incredible challenge for BBC Children in Need, cycling 400 miles through all four nations.

"As you set off in Glasgow, I just want to say: 'Let's Go, Owain!' We'll be cheering you on all the way. Good luck."

She sent him another message when he finished, saying: "Congratulations on completing your incredible challenge for Children in Need. You're still the one my friend, sending you all my love."

Helen Thomas, head of Radio 2, said: "Owain truly captured the hearts of the nation this week as he battled through his epic four nations challenge.

"On behalf of all the Radio 2 listeners as well as the thousands of children and families who will benefit from his Herculean fundraising efforts we simply can't thank him enough. Diolch Owain! "

Evans began his broadcasting career in Welsh-language television when he presented the children's news programme Ffeil.

He later presented the weather on BBC Wales Today and began hosting BBC Radio 2's Early Breakfast Show in 2023.

MN202611_1x4dw65hm7v.t:
Umunyamabanga Mukuru w’Umuryango Mpuzamahanga w’Ibihugu bikoresha Igifaransa (OIF), Louise Mushikiwabo, yavuze ko Francophonie ari urubuga rukomeye ruhuza abantu n’ibihugu bifite amateka n’imico bitandukanye, rukabafasha gusangira ubumenyi, guteza imbere ubufatanye no kubaka amahoro.

Yabigarutseho kuri uyu wa 13 Ugushyingo 2026, ubwo yafunguraga ku mugaragaro Igikorwa cyiswe Village de la Francophonie, kiri kubera i Phnom Penh, mu murwa mukuru wa Cambodia, mu rwego rwo gutegura Inama ya 20 y’Abakuru b’Ibihugu na Guverinoma bigize Francophonie.

Mushikiwabo yavuze ko iki gikorwa gifite uruhare rukomeye mu kwerekana ubudasa bw’imico n’ubukungu by’ibihugu bigize uyu muryango, aho ibihugu byo ku migabane itanu byitabiriye bifite aho bigaragariza umuco, amateka n’ibyo byagezeho.

Yagize ati: “Iki gikorwa ni ikindi kimenyetso cy’uko iki gihugu cyiza cya Cambodia gifite isano ikomeye na Francophonie, ndetse n’icyifuzo cyacyo cyo guhindura iyi nama umunsi mukuru ukomeye, ufunguye kuri buri wese.”

Yongeyeho ko Francophonie idakwiye kugarukira gusa ku nama za dipolomasi n’ibiganiro bya politiki, ahubwo ko ari n’umwanya wo guhuza abaturage, bagasangira ubunararibonye kandi bakishimira ubudasa bwabo.

Mushikiwabo kandi yagaragaje isano iri hagati ya Cambodia n’u Rwanda, avuga ko ibihugu byombi bifite amateka n’umurage ndangamuco ukomeye, abaturage bagaragaje ubudahangarwa mu bihe bikomeye ndetse n’icyerekezo cyo kubaka ejo hazaza harangwa n’amahoro n’iterambere.

Yashimangiye ko umuziki n’imbyino ari zimwe mu nzira zikomeye zihuza abantu baturuka mu bihugu bitandukanye, nubwo baba batandukanijwe n'intera ndende.

Ati: “Izi ni zo mbaraga za Francophonie: guhuza abantu, amateka n’imyumvire bitandukanye, ubusanzwe bitari kugira amahirwe yo guhura.”

Yavuze ko iki gikorwa ari n’umwanya mwiza wo kumenyekanisha Francophonie mu Banyacambodia, ariko nanone ugafasha abaturage bo mu bihugu bikoresha Igifaransa kumenya Cambodia n’umurage wayo.

Mushikiwabo yongeyeho ko gukoresha indimi z’Igifaransa n’Igikhmer bishobora gufasha kubaka imibanire mishya no guteza imbere ubufatanye hagati y’ibihugu.

Igikorwa cyo gufungura Village de la Francophonie cyaranzwe n’imbyino n’ibindi bikorwa ndangamuco by’abahanzi bo muri Cambodia n’Abanyarwanda bo mu Itorero ry’Igihugu, bigaragaza ubufatanye bw’umuco w’ibihugu byombi.

Iki gikorwa kizakomeza kugeza ku wa 17 Ugushyingo 2026, kikaba giteganyijwe kwakira abantu bagera ku 100.000 baturutse muri Cambodia no mu bindi bihugu.

Inama ya 20 ya Francophonie igiye kubera i Phnom Penh Inama ya 20 y’Abakuru b’Ibihugu na Guverinoma bigize Francophonie iteganyijwe kubera i Phnom Penh ku wa 15 n'uwa 16 Ugushyingo 2026.

Izitabirwa n’abayobozi bahagarariye ibihugu na za Guverinoma 90 bigize uyu muryango, bakazaganira ku bufatanye mu bya politiki, ubukungu, umuco, uburezi n’ibindi bibazo bireba umuryango mpuzamahanga.

Insanganyamatsiko yayo igira iti: “Kongera gushora imbaraga mu mahoro kugira ngo haboneke iterambere risangiwe n’umutekano urambye.”

Iyi nsanganyamatsiko ije mu gihe Francophonie ishimangira ko amahoro ari umusingi w’iterambere rirambye. Mu itangazo ry’Umuryango OIF ryo ku wa 10 Ugushyingo, Mushikiwabo yavuze ko amahoro ari umutungo wubakwa buhoro buhoro, ariko ushobora kwangirika vuba kandi ugasaba kwitabwaho buri munsi.

Yagaragaje ko Cambodia, yanyuze mu bihe bikomeye mu mateka yayo ikongera kwiyubaka, izi neza agaciro k’amahoro.

Iyi nama kandi izaba umwanya wo gutora Umunyamabanga Mukuru mushya wa Francophonie cyangwa kongerera manda uriho, uzayobora uyu muryango mu gihe cy'imyaka itau iri imbere (2027–2030). Abakandida bane bahatanye barimo na Louise Mushikiwabo uhagarariye u Rwanda.

Mbere y’inama nyirizina, ku wa 14 Ugushyingo hazaba inama ya 48 y’Abaminisitiri ba Francophonie.

Uretse ibiganiro bya politiki, hazaba n’imurikabikorwa rya FrancoTech ryibanda ku ikoranabuhanga n’udushya, ndetse n’ibindi bikorwa bigamije guteza imbere ubucuruzi, umuco n’imikoranire hagati y’abaturage bo mu bihugu bigize Francophonie.

MN202611_9fbrc24nsw.t:
The site of a car explosion that wounded Sergei Zavorotny in Moscow

A car bomb attack in Moscow has wounded a former adviser to Ukrainian ex-prime minister Mykola Azarov, Russia's Investigative Committee says.

Sergei Zavorotny, now a journalist and commentator, was behind the wheel of his black Toyota when the explosion happened and Azarov told Russian TV his condition in hospital was "rather critical".

The car bomb went off a day after a Russian colonel was killed in another explosion in St Petersburg, and both blasts are seen as part of a series of attacks on military and prominent figures linked to Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

Zavorotny, 72, worked as a press aide to Mykola Azarov in Kyiv until 2014.

But when pro-Kremlin Ukrainian president Viktor Yanukovych was toppled from power, Azarov fled Kyiv for Russia and tried unsuccessfully to set up a government in exile.

In a 2020 US Senate report on interference in the 2016 American presidential election, Zavorotny is described at the time as an SVR [Russian foreign intelligence] officer involved in influence operations.

Russia's Investigative Committee said on Telegram on Friday: "Serhiy Zavorotny, a former adviser to the former Ukrainian Prime Minister Mykola Azarov, was injured while driving a car. He was taken to one of the city hospitals, where he is receiving medical care."

It added: "A set of necessary investigative actions is being carried out. A number of examinations will be appointed, including medical and explosives."

According to several unconfirmed reports, Zavorotny suffered a number of serious injuries after an explosive device was detonated remotely.

Russia said the car bombs are the latest in a series of attacks targeting pro-Kremlin figures.

On Thursday a car bomb in the Pushkinsky District of St Petersburg killed a member of the Russian military, again after it was attached to the base of the car and detonated remotely.

The man targeted in the attack is yet to be named officially, but reputable sources suggest he was a high-ranking figure in the 6th Guards Air and Air Defence Forces Army.

Overnight into Friday, Ukraine and Russia exchanged attacks on each other's territories.

Ukrainian authorities said a hospital had been targeted by Russian bombardment.

They added that three people, including a 17-year-old boy, were also killed in attacks across southern Odesa and Zaporizhzhia.

Russia said a Ukrainian strike on an industrial facility in the central Samara region killed four people.

And in the southern Volgograd region another four died after an industrial zone was hit by drones. A further person died in the Bryansk border region, an area that is often fired upon.

Ukraine said these were retaliatory attacks in response to Russia's persistent targeting of its cities.

Aya makuru yari amaze iminsi avugwa, Manchester United yayemeje ibinyujije ku mbugankoranyambaga zayo aho yavuze ko bumvikanye n'Ishyiramwe ry'Umupira w'Amaguru muri Leta Zunze Ubumwe za Amerika nk'igihugu yatozaga, kuzarekura uyu mugabo w'imyaka 54 y'amavuko ndetse n'itsinda akorana naryo, ubwo bazaba basoje imikino iki gihugu gifite muri uku kwezi ku Ugushyingo 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino yatangiye gutoza mu 2009 ahereye muri Espagnol muri Espagne, mu 2013 atoza Southampton umwaka umwe, ajya muri Tottenham Hotspurs mu 2019 kugeza 2019 ubwo yayivagambo ayigejeje ku mukino wa nyuma wa UEFA Champions League agatsindwa na Liverpool 2-0.

Mauricio Pochettino asimbuye Michael Carrick wirukanwe na Manchester United, aho yabyemeje ku wa Kane w'iki cyumweru nyuma yo kuyitoza nk'umutoza w’agateganyo igice cy'umwaka w'imikino 2025-2026 ahereye muri Mutarama 2026, maze mu mpeshyi y'uyu mwaka agahabwa amasezerano yari kuzageza mu 2028.

MN202611_1wavtegnqt2.t:
Arsenal's Premier League-winning captain Martin Odegaard also wears the armband for Norway

Martin Odegaard admits snow disruption has affected Norway's preparations for Saturday's Nations League meeting with Wales – but the Arsenal captain is backing his team to avenge their defeat in Cardiff last month.

Wales beat the World Cup quarter-finalists 2-1 for their only win of the campaign so far, with Norway head coach Stale Solbakken describing the first-half performance as their worst for two years.

Norway had to train indoors on Thursday because the Ullevaal Stadion pitch, which was criticised earlier this year before being repaired in the summer, was covered in snow.

That snow was cleared on Friday, allowing Norway to resume training in Oslo as they look to climb off the bottom of Group A4.

How do you stop Haaland? Wales show how it's done

Wales' James warns of Norwegian revenge in Oslo

They have three points out of six from four games, the same tally as Wales, but are below Craig Bellamy's side in third because of their head-to-head record.

"Obviously we wanted to train yesterday, so it's not ideal but you have to adapt to the situation, and I think it's not the end of the world," Odegaard said.

On the defeat in Wales, the Arsenal midfielder added: "Our level was not where it should be. I think it's probably the only game for a long time where we haven't been playing to our standards.

"Wales is a good team, a competitive team, lots of good players in big leagues and a physical team as well, and we were prepared for that.

"But I think on the day we were just not showing up to our standards and that's something we want to show tomorrow [Saturday], and we can do a lot better. We want to show a different version tomorrow."

Live on BBC iPlayer, BBC Two Wales, BBC Sounds, BBC Radio Wales, Radio Cymru and 5 Live Sports Extra, BBC Sport website and app, plus live text commentary.

Having been unbeaten in 2025 before impressing with their run to the last eight at this summer's World Cup, Norway have lost their past three matches , with 2-1 defeats against Portugal either side of their loss by the same score in Cardiff.

Norway and Wales still have a chance of finishing second behind Portugal, but they are also battling each other to avoid potential relegation from the Nations League's top tier.

"It's like a boxing game, going head-to-head, fist-to-fist," said Solbakken.

"I think Wales has always been a very attacking team under Bellamy. They've had great progress with the ball.

"I think it suits the team with the offensive players they have, the speed on the wings and Harry Wilson back. And [Lewis] Koumas getting more minutes for Liverpool, so I think that suits them.

"I'm not surprised that they will go all in but it's our home game so obviously I think they will also have their struggles with us. Let's see."

Wales head coach Bellamy and winger Daniel James, who scored their first goal in Cardiff last month, have said they are mindful of Norway's desire to exact revenge.

Asked if that was an incentive for his side, Solbakken said: "I think both teams need to win the game, so you can call it revenge or whatever.

"I think we were very passive in the first half against Wales. We had no intensity in our play. We were decent with the ball, but we were crap without the ball.

"Overall, they deserved to lead by half-time and then there was our red card one minute into the second half.

"I think the first half was our worst performance in two years, we have to be honest about that.

"It's two aims for us now in this football year. That is to at least be going for the third place first, and that we can do tomorrow. It's a crucial game."

MN202611_tdogp8hd62.t:
The nuclear agency has not been able to inspect any sites attacked by the US and Israel last year

The UN's nuclear watchdog has said it is "increasingly concerned" about a nuclear facility in Iran which it has not been allowed to inspect.

Iran informed the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) of plans to set up the uranium enrichment plant in the city of Isfahan a day before Israel began attacking its nuclear sites last June. The US joined the strikes later that month.

In a report seen by news agencies, the IAEA said it does not know the exact location or whether it contains nuclear material.

Since the start of the latest war, Iran has restricted IAEA inspectors' access to its nuclear sites, preventing the agency from verifying its enriched uranium stockpile.

Under a 2015 nuclear deal, Iran agreed to limit its enriched uranium stockpile to 300kg and enrichment to 3.67% purity. It subsequently exceeded both.

Before the June 2025 strikes, it had accumulated an estimated 441kg enriched to 60%, close to weapons grade.

The nuclear complex at Isfahan suffered extensive damage in US and Israeli strikes, particularly the parts above the ground. The condition of its underground facilities is not clear.

The IAEA believes much of Iran's highly enriched uranium was stored there.

"The Agency's lack of information about [Iran's] nuclear material and access to facilities to verify it is a matter of serious proliferation concern... and needs to be rectified with the utmost urgency," it said in the latest report.

Iran announced plans for the Isfahan Fuel Enrichment Plant (IFEP) on 12 June 2025, shortly after an IAEA resolution which declared Iran had failed to meet its nuclear safeguards obligations.

Iran initially agreed to allow inspectors to visit the facility, but the inspection was cancelled after Israel launched attacks the following day.

The IAEA's latest calls come almost a year after it made a similar appeal to Iran. At the time it said it had only inspected some of the 13 nuclear facilities that were "unaffected" by the attacks and none of the seven that were.

The US and Israel said they attacked Iran's nuclear sites to prevent it developing nuclear weapons - something Iran has consistently denied seeking. It says its nuclear programme is for peaceful civilian purposes only.

MN202611_15klzlddwzz.t:
Kalajdzic came off the bench to score the winner for Austria

Republic of Ireland's hopes of securing top spot and automatic promotion to League A were ended by Austria after they suffered a 1-0 defeat in their penultimate Nations League Group B3 game at the Raiffeisen Arena.

Substitute Sasa Kalajdzic poked home from a corner to score the winner on 79 minutes as Austria preserved their unbeaten home record, which stretches back to October 2023.

The defeat in Linz, Republic of Ireland's second away loss in the group, leaves Heimir Hallgrimsson's side third, a point behind Kosovo, who they face in their final game on Tuesday.

A win in that fixture in Dublin would ensure a second-place finish and Republic of Ireland's place in pot two for the Euro 2028 qualifying draw in December.

Austria, who fought back from two goals down to take a point against the Irish in Dublin last month, started well and tested Caoimhin Kelleher just two minutes in as he was forced to get down low to turn Christoph Baumgartner's deflected strike behind.

The Irish grew into the game and threatened for the first time on 22 minutes as Troy Parrott connected with Dara O'Shea's delivery from the left, but his acrobatic effort was dealt with by Alexander Schlager.

The Real Betis striker went close again soon after when his rising strike from range was tipped over by the goalkeeper.

At the other end, Kelleher produced a fine reflex save to push Christoph Lang's half-volley over the crossbar before Michael Gregoritsch, who scored in the 2-2 draw in Dublin, then blasted over.

Austria continued to push for the opener in the second half as Gregoritsch's glancing header from a corner landed on the roof of the net and Kelleher then made two good saves to thwart Kevin Danso and Baumgartner.

The RB Leipzig midfielder looked certain to break the deadlock after the hour mark when he raced into the box, but skewed a shot horribly wide.

Momentum shifted back to Republic of Ireland in this end-to-end encounter as Ryan Manning and Parrott both drew flying saves from Schlager.

Gregoritsch's fizzing strike from a short free-kick routine was saved by Kelleher, before the hosts did make a spell of sustained pressure count 11 minutes from time.

Gregoritsch met a deep corner and headed the ball back across goal, with Kelleher only able to push the ball into the path of Kalajdzic, who stabbed home on the line.

Substitute Chiedozie Ogbene squandered a golden chance to equalise on 86 minutes as he headed straight at Schlager after connecting with Liam Scales' super ball in as the Irish left Linz empty handed.

Republic of Ireland have won just one of their five Nations League games

Hallgrimsson spoke in the build-up to the game that he wanted his side to cut out mistakes and be braver in Linz.

He emphasised that second point by selecting an attack-minded line-up.

Finn Azaz dropped into a deeper roll to accommodate Adam Idah and Jack Moylan behind Parrott after the three linked so well in the 3-0 win over Israel, as the Irish chased a victory which would keep their hopes of winning the group alive.

After a shaky opening, Hallgrimsson's side settled and produced a spirited display, but they ultimately lacked the clinical edge to finish any of the numerous opportunities they created.

Their talisman Parrott, who had 10 goals in his last seven competitive games but is without a goal in eight for his club, failed to beat Schlager with his three clear-cut chances while Idah and Moylan cut peripheral figures in a frustrating evening in front of goal.

The ever-reliable Kelleher kept the Irish in the game at times with some big saves in an entertaining game, but he was powerless to stop Kalajdzic's winning goal.

Hallgrimsson will be frustrated his side failed to deal with the corner before it fell to Kalajdzic to score, which was ultimately the defining moment in a tight game.

They pressed hard for a late leveller, with Austria hanging on at times, but Ogbene's late miss cost them a point.

Republic of Ireland will take confidence from how well they competed with Austria across the two games, but to come away with just a point having played well home and away, will be tough to take.

Their hopes of trying to win promotion to League A for the first time are not all lost, but they now must produce against Kosovo, who they suffered defeat against last month, to secure second place and a promotion play-off, which would have been the aim heading into this campaign.

MN202611_v9t162lxmw.t:
How could the Nvidia CEO’s affair threaten US national security?

How close is Donald Trump to Jensen Huang?

The Nvidia boss was one of the few business leaders with direct access to the US president. He had met Trump repeatedly, travelled with him to Britain and, in May, joined him on Air Force One for his trip to China.

Jensen Huang wasn't just another tech billionaire seeking the president's ear. He had become an important voice in one of the biggest arguments inside the administration: how much of America's most advanced technology should be allowed to reach China.

Nvidia makes the chips that power the AI revolution. Washington has restricted exports of its most advanced processors to China since 2022, believing they could help Beijing develop its military and technological capabilities.

But enforcing those restrictions is difficult. Chips can be bought legally by customers in countries such as Singapore and Malaysia and then diverted to China. Chinese companies can also rent access to computing power through data centres outside the country.

Jensen Huang has long argued that the restrictions are counterproductive. They shut Nvidia out of a huge market and encourage Chinese companies to develop their own alternatives. Trump appeared sympathetic to this view, allowing Nvidia to resume sales of certain chips to China last year in return for a share of the revenue, although its most advanced Blackwell chips remain off limits.

But that relationship now looks rather more complicated.

The allegations surrounding Jensen Huang's reported affair with Alice Huang, of no relation but a former executive at Singapore-based company Megaspeed, have raised the possibility that a foreign intelligence operation was targeting not just a powerful businessman, but someone with unusually close access to the American president.

US intelligence reportedly suspects Alice Huang of having links to Chinese intelligence. Beijing has rejected the allegations. Nvidia's board says it has no reason to believe company secrets or national security were compromised. But the affair has opened up a much bigger question: what did the administration in Washington know, and what did it do about it?

That question leads directly to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.

His department was responsible for controlling exports of sensitive American technology. It was also being pressed to act on concerns about Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer suspected of helping divert advanced chips to China.

On Thursday, Megaspeed chief executive, Tan Yong Pong, also known as James Tan, said the company "takes its compliance obligations under US export control laws extremely seriously" and is "committed to working constructively and transparently with the US government". He said the company had co-operated with US Commerce Department inspections.

A highly classified memo was shared with Lutnick about the concerns surrounding Alice Huang and Megaspeed. He resisted taking action against the company, a decision that is now under scrutiny.

Other senior officials wanted a tougher response.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was among those who reportedly questioned why Megaspeed had not been placed on the Commerce Department's blacklist.

On Friday, Bessent pointed the finger at Commerce for not blacklisting the company, telling CNBC that several government agencies "were in favour of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months".

"But Commerce has the pen... and you will have to ask them about their internal process," he added.

There have also been questions about why an investigation into the Singapore-based company was stopped after Nvidia intervened. The New York Times reported that Nvidia's general counsel contacted Commerce Department investigators probing suspected chip smuggling by Megaspeed invoking a senior Trump appointee. The department allegedly then froze its investigation and handed the case to the Justice Department.

This apparently highlighted a significant disagreement about the direction of Trump's China policy. Huang wanted access to the Chinese market. Other officials were supposedly worried about the national security consequences. Lutnick was caught in the middle.

Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned to testify before Congress about affair with alleged Chinese spy

Bessent blames Lutnick's Commerce Department for failing to block Megaspeed

Members of Congress from both parties want answers. Democrats have launched an investigation into how the Commerce Department vetted Chinese companies approved to buy AI chips. Republicans are also questioning the administration's approach.

And Jensen Huang's departure has not eased the pressure.

Republican representative John Moolenaar, who chairs the House Select Committee on China, said it was in the national interest for Nvidia and other American AI firms to succeed, but that companies "should never jeopardise our nation's security" by giving Chinese firms access to their most advanced chips.

Senator Elizabeth Warren, the top Democrat on the Senate Banking Committee, said Huang's resignation did not absolve him of responsibility, and urged Lutnick to explain why export control loopholes remain open.

Meanwhile Jensen Huang's team told Republican lawmakers on Wednesday that he plans to cooperate with their request to testify behind closed doors.

The White House has not responded to the BBC's request for comment.

It has, however, told the New York Post that Trump has complete confidence in Lutnick, describing him as "the most transformative commerce secretary in modern history".

That is a fairly emphatic show of support, particularly amid reports that officials are weighing whether Lutnick should be forced out.

There are some obvious questions. If Lutnick had indeed been warned about the risks, why did his department fail to act? And if other senior officials were indeed pressing for action, why did it take so long?

The BBC has contacted the Commerce Department for comment. But there is an even bigger question for Trump.

The president cultivated a close relationship with Huang. He was directly involved in decisions about chip sales to China. And, according to reporting in the New York Times, he was briefed on the intelligence concerns.

This is becoming difficult to dismiss as the misjudgement of one businessman or one government department.

Jensen Huang's personal life may have triggered the crisis, but the questions now reach into the White House itself. How much influence did he have? What did the president know? And who was ultimately responsible for protecting America's most sensitive technology?

MN202611_1ied0b85ws2.t:
Warning - this story contains graphic content

More women have come forward to make allegations about disgraced entertainer Russell Brand, in interviews with the Times and a new Netflix documentary.

Brand was jailed earlier this week after being found guilty of one count of rape and three of sexual assault at a trial in London.

Allegations against him first emerged after an investigation by the Times, the Sunday Times and Channel 4's Dispatches in 2023.

The Times has now reported , external accusations of what it called sexual misconduct and predatory behaviour by a further six women, which the newspaper said could not be reported until the criminal case had ended. He has denied non-consensual sexual activity.

The Times report was published on Thursday evening, and a Netflix documentary, titled Russell Brand: Open Secret, was made available on Friday morning.

The programme included an interview with a woman referred to as Emily, not her real name, who said she was in a relationship with Brand when she was in her twenties.

On one occasion, she said she "literally begged" Brand to stop after he refused to wear a condom during sex.

Emily, who was portrayed by an actress in the documentary, said: "I said to him, 'No, Russell, please, let's just use protection.' I kept saying 'No'. I said, 'Stop Russell, stop, please don't, please.'

"I begged him. I literally begged him. I tried to kick him off, I tried to draw my knees back, to kick him in his belly, but he was too strong for me."

But he "just pinned my hands back behind my head" before forcing himself upon her, she alleged.

"When it happens you just feel like, is this... is this rape? Because I'm with this guy [in a relationship]," she said, according to the documentary.

"I know I said 'No', but you question yourself and you think, did I do something wrong?"

She "left his as quickly as I could" and told one friend what had happened, but "back then women felt shamed", she said.

"You didn't talk about it. I just felt completely violated and unseen and unheard. I was saying 'No'. I kept saying, 'No, stop, please, stop, stop, no'."

Brand will face 'hell on earth' in Wandsworth prison, says former inmate

Met Police investigating more 'potential criminal allegations' about Brand

Russell Brand being investigated over rape allegations from two more women, police say

Another ex-girlfriend, Jordan Martin, claimed in the documentary that Brand sexually assaulted her and smashed her phone in a hotel after she had spoken to an ex to arrange to collect her belongings.

"He snatched my phone out of my hand and broke it apart into pieces," she said.

Brand then followed her into a different room, she said. "He didn't say anything. He put his hand down the front of my jeans and he inserted a finger and then he walked away."

She added: "I look at myself back then and I feel sorry for myself. And not in a bad or pitying way, I just feel like it wasn't very fair."

Martin also said Brand was jealous and controlling, and had made her "brush her teeth until gums bled".

"He wanted me to taste anonymous," Martin said. "And so he was asking me to brush my teeth, but it just was never enough. And so he's standing over me and I'm brushing and I'm brushing, and then I'm seeing my teeth bleeding."

The Times and Sunday Times reported that at least five sexual partners said Brand had forced them to brush their teeth, including the fifth complainant in the trial, whom he was convicted of raping in 2009.

Among the new claims reported by the paper is one from a woman referred to as Alex, who claimed she had asked Brand to stop having sex after noticing he wasn't using a condom.

"I said, 'No, stop', and I started to sort of try and move. And... that wasn't happening," she said.

When he continued, she decided "I'm not going to fight", she said, because "who knows what he could do?"

Alex said Brand apologised in person and by text message after the alleged incident.

"I justified it in my head by saying to myself, at least he admitted it," she told the Times.

A woman called Vicky also claimed she had asked him to stop twice after they started having sex without any build up.

"My body wasn't ready for this and it was painful", she remembered.

"An uneasy wave hits me and I'm scared. And I say, 'It's painful' and he doesn't stop. And then it gets worse and it's really painful. And I say 'Stop' and he doesn't stop."

She added that it had felt like he "just wasn't present".

She claimed he said afterwards: "Tonight was consensual. Nobody did anything they didn't want to do."

Another woman named Zoe said Brand was "annoyed" after she turned up to his hotel late.

"He basically sort of just grabbed me and manhandled me around a little bit and he put his hand on my throat," she told the Times.

"And then he shoved his other hand down my trousers and penetrated me with his finger.

"I didn't resist. I just sort of let it happen."

On Monday, Brand was sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison following his trial. He is expected to serve seven years.

He denied the charges and was acquitted on two further rape charges and one count of attempted indecent assault.

Police have said Brand is being investigated over rape allegations made by two more women.

The Metropolitan Police have said they are also "assessing" information from several people who contacted them during the trial "to provide information or report a potential criminal allegation".

Brand has been placed inside HMP Wandsworth . BBC News has asked his legal representatives for a response to the latest allegations.

MN202611_w0pxnxodl.t:
Police Scotland said a man had died at FirstStage studios in Leith

A member of the crew for the Netflix series Dept Q has died after being seriously injured at a film studio in Edinburgh.

Emergency crews were called to FirstStage studio in Leith at about 15:00 on Thursday and the man was pronounced dead a short time later.

Left Bank Pictures, which is involved in making Dept Q, later said it was "shocked and saddened" by the death of a crew member.

Police Scotland said the death was not being treated as suspicious but inquiries into the circumstances were ongoing. The Health and Safety Executive said it was "aware" of the incident.

A Left Bank Pictures spokesperson said: "We are deeply shocked and saddened by the tragic death of a member of our Dept Q crew.

"Our thoughts are with their family, friends and colleagues at this incredibly difficult time, and we are offering support for those affected."

'It's a big step up': Behind the scenes as Netflix hit Dept Q returns to Edinburgh

FirstStage was started by Sean Connery's son, Jason, and took over an empty former warehouse unit in Leith in 2020.

The "big blue shed" includes five sound stages and production office space.

Screen Scotland invested £1m towards the initial set up of the facility.

Aside from Dept Q, it has also been used for filming the supernatural thriller The Rig for Amazon, and for part of the production of Marvel's Avengers: Infinity War, which was partially set in Edinburgh.

Mayors from French speaking countries have explored the contentious border dispute between Cambodia and Thailand.

Taarifa political desk has learned that a delegation from the International Association of Francophone Mayors (AIMF) and its partners, led by AIMF Delegate General Frederic Vallier Thursday met with Phnom Penh city Governor Khuong Sreng to discuss cooperation and the situation along the Cambodia-Thailand border.

Sreng said, “in the 21st century, no country should invade another or destroy cultural heritage of global significance.”

Between July and December 2025, Cambodia and Thailand military fell out over disputed border.

The clashes resulted in severe destruction to the UNESCO World Heritage site Preah Vihear Temple and the 800-year old Ta Kwai (Ta Krabey) Temples along the border.

Cambodia condemned the strikes as a “barbaric” violation of cultural heritage, while the Thai Second Army Region maintained that Cambodian forces had occupied the ruins as a military position.

In connection with the 20th Francophonie Summit being hosted in Cambodia, Vallier said the AIMF would organise several side events in cooperation with the capital’s administration.

These include a regional conference for mayors and local government representatives under the theme “City Diplomacy for Peace and Local Development”.

MN202611_13aj1skby9e.t:
Some bin collections were missed partly because of the heatwave

Some bin collections were missed over the summer in a county partly because the heatwave became so serious it posed a risk to the lives of workers, a council worker has said.

Flintshire County Council's Chris Goddard said crews faced a "perfect storm" of challenges during the UK's record-breaking hot weather , causing a spate of widespread missed collections.

During the summer, drought was declared in all of Wales and wildfires caused devastation in parts of the country .

Goddard said: "We do have to make some difficult decisions but ultimately if there is a fatality in the workplace because of a decision I've made, that's something that I would have to live with - and probably defend."

Despite the missed collections the council remained on target to hit the Welsh government's national 70% waste recycling target this year, the Local Democracy Reporting Service said.

Flintshire County Council is on track to hit its waste recycling target despite the disruption

Goddard, the council's streetscene service manager, said: "We had maybe five or six operational challenges that all came at the same time in a perfect storm this summer.

"Unfortunately, the heatwave was one of them and it was a contributing factor. We do have to prioritise staff safety above all else.

"My number one job every day is to make sure that everybody goes home safely and we take that really seriously within streetscene. That was only one of several contributing factors.

"That level of change is naturally going to cause a few bumps in the road, particularly with staff being asked to do a little bit more. There were some staffing issues during that period too."

Councillors praised Flintshire residents for largely embracing three-weekly residual waste collections and ensuring that the authority remained on-target to hit its statutory recycling rate.

"Three-weekly was very controversial at the time it came in," said Saltney councillor Richard Lloyd.

"It's quite clear to see now that the three-weekly black bin collection has been a good new factor. Recycling has improved at the kerbside."

Councillors said in the authority's meeting the change to three-weekly bin collections meant the council should still hit target despite the disruption.

The council also cut the amount of waste it sent to landfill or Parc Adfer by 6,467.49 tonnes between 2024 and 2026, and that improvement continued this year despite problems this summer.

Rwanda and Cambodia have opened a new chapter in their cooperation after signing agreements covering investment, tourism and air services on Friday.

President Kagame of Rwanda and Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet witnessed the signing of the agreements.

The three documents include a Memorandum of Understanding between the Council for the Development of Cambodia (CDC) and the Rwanda Development Board (RDB) an MoU on cooperation in the tourism sector and an Air Services Agreement.

MN202611_li9it02f9u.t:
Rosalía released her fourth album Lux last year to rave reviews

Spanish star Rosalía has made history as the first woman to win the best album award at the Latin Grammys three times, after being recognised for her project Lux.

The singer took home five trophies in total, including two for her track La Perla which was named song of the year and best pop song.

La Perla was also nominated for record of the year but missed out to Argentine singer Milo J's song Niño.

Rosalía released Lux last year to rave reviews and collecting her award at the ceremony in Las Vegas on Thursday, she said: "To all the people who told me I wasn't good enough, or that my music was too weird, I'm thankful I didn't listen."

The Barcelona-born artist then added: "Now I'm winning these prizes."

Rosalía, who opened the ceremony with a performance of some of her biggest songs, was honoured with the prize for best alternative music album.

She also picked up best shortform music video for her track Sauvignon Blanc.

The singer had previously won best album for El Mal Querer in 2019 and Motomami in 2022 - and her third Lux is also tipped to be a favourite when nominations are announced for the Grammys next week.

After a career spanning three decades, Daddy Yankee was recognised with a lifetime achievement award

It was also a big night for Puerto Rican reggaeton legend Daddy Yankee, who won the person of the year award.

He performed some of his best-loved tracks including Gasolina and Con Calma, and was joined on stage by rappers including LL Cool J and French Montana.

Punjabi singer Diljit Dosanjh, who collabed with Daddy Yankee on Pokito, even took a break from his Aura India tour for the set, making him the first Indian artist to perform at the Latin Grammys.

Dosanjh superfan Devanshi Arora described the singer's appearance as "a cultural revolution".

"It's really invigorating and motivating to see someone from my country has made it all around the world," she tells Newsbeat.

She sees a lot of similarities between South American and Punjabi communities and hopes this leads to more collaborations - with a link-up between Dosanjh and Bad Bunny top of her wishlist.

Daddy Yankee was presented with the lifetime achievement award by Janet Jackson, who told him in Spanish that his music "has inspired an entire generation".

Diljit Dosanjh became the first Indian artist to perform at the Latin Grammys

Accepting the prize for record of the year, Milo J seemed surprised to have won ahead of strong competition from Karol G, Jorge Drexler, Carin León as well as Rosalía.

The 20-year-old took home four trophies in the end and gave a shout out to Argentine folk music.

He described Niño as the song "I'm most proud of out of everything I've created so far".

"Long live Argentine folk music," he added.

Elsewhere, ARIA VEGA was named best new artist and songwriter of the year went to Sara Schell.

MN202611_flmnstfk9n.t:
All parties have been banned at the university

Four Nigerian students have died after attending a party in the south-eastern town of Nsukka to celebrate the end of their final exams.

The cause of death has not been confirmed but police spokesman Daniel Ndukwe said the two men and two women had reportedly fallen ill after consuming alcoholic drinks at the party.

The University of Nigeria Nsukka has declared three days of mourning, during which academic and social activities will be suspended.

The tragedy comes amid a wider crackdown on fake and adulterated alcoholic drinks in Nigeria, where the food and drug regulator has been raiding suspected producers of unsafe food and beverages.

The university's Vice-Chancellor, Professor Simon Ortuanya, said the university had received a distress call at 22:00 on Wednesday, and sent security personnel to a house party at Praise Lodge, outside the campus in Nsukka's Hilltop area.

"The preliminary investigation and interim report point to alleged alcohol abuse or drug paraphernalia and things like that. But we are not conclusive on those matters," he said.

He described the deaths as "tragic and painful".

"As a community, we mourn, not just alone, we mourn with the families, the parents that have suffered these years to train the men and women in their studies," he said.

Ortuanya also announced a ban on signing-out celebrations, which are commonly held by final-year students to mark the completion of their studies.

The celebrations often involve parties, dancing, photographs and friends signing one another's shirts. He urged students to use graduation as a time to reflect on their university experience and prepare for life beyond campus.

The university said it was working with security agencies to establish what had caused the deaths.

The police have also launched an investigation. They said alcoholic drinks had been recovered from the scene and the bodies taken to a mortuary for autopsies.

The investigation comes amid wider concerns about unsafe alcoholic drinks in Nigeria.

In September, dozens of people fell ill after consuming locally made alcoholic drinks and herbal mixtures in communities across Ondo State, south-west Nigeria.

More than 11 people died in the Araromi-Obu area, while more than 50 others were hospitalised.

Investigations found that some of the drinks had been contaminated with methanol, a highly toxic form of alcohol that can cause blindness and death.

Nigeria's food and drug regulator, Nafdac, reported more than 150 cases, including 48 confirmed deaths. More than 80 people were hospitalised, and five lost their sight.

The regulator has been carrying out raids across the country, targeting facilities suspected of producing fake or adulterated alcoholic drinks, food and beverages.

Nigeria has long struggled with the sale of unsafe and adulterated products, which campaigners warn pose a serious threat to public health.
