MN202611_czf3xb80e5.t:
Cambodia said on Wednesday that alcohol consumption puts the country into losses valued at over U$1billion annually.

According to a research Report presented to government, it is estimated that alcohol consumption drained U$1 billion annually, accounting for roughly 2% of gross domestic product.

The study showed that in Cambodia drinking households faced heavier debt burdens, family disputes and disruptions to children’s education.

These research findings are obtained from a study across Cambodia’s 12 municipal and provincial areas involving 2,549 households.

Cambodia government is being pushed to fast-track the draft law on alcohol control to protect youth, women and children.

On Wednesday Cambodia held a national conference on alcohol policy bringing together government officials, civil society groups and researchers to build consensus on the proposed legislation.

It was recommended that enacting the legislation would tighten advertising controls, regulate sale hours and locations, and adding alcohol education to school curricula.

MN202611_l00i0ptehj.t:
Roseanna Hall, umukobwa aserukira Zimbabwe mw'ihiganwa Miss Universe, hamwe n'abandi baserukira ibihugu bimwe bimwe vya Afrika, boshobora kutitaba ihiganwa ry'uyu mwaka rizobera muri Puerto Rico, mu gihe bariko bararwana, mu buryo butoroshe, no kurondera impusha zo kwinjira muri Amerika.

Hall ategekanya guhagararira Zimbabwe muri iryo higanwa Miss Universe rizoba ribaye ku ncuro ya 75, aho uwuzotsinda azokwambikwa urugori ku wa 24 Munyonyo (11). Ariko, ntararonka uruhusha rwo kuja muri Puerto Rico, akarere gakukira Amerika.

Mu butumwa yacishije kuri konte yiwe ya instagram, yagize ati: "Tumaze imisi tugenda tugaruka, tugerageza kuronka uruhusha rwo kuja muri Amerika rwemewe."

Hall si we wenyene mu bahiganwa b'Abanyafrika bakozweko n'ingingo yo kugabanya abarekuriwe kwinjira muri Amerika. Igihugu ca Zambia carakuye muri iryo higanwa uwari kugiserukira, Pamela Mubanga, kubera ingingo Amerika yafashe zitorohereza ingenzi ziva mu bihugu bimwe bimwe kwinjira ku butaka bwayo.

Abahiganwa batanguye gushika muri Puerto Rico kuva ku wa 8 Munyonyo (11), kugira biyandikishe, bapimwe impuzu bazokwambara hamwe n'ibindi bikorwa bitegurwa imbere y'uko ihiganwa ritangura. Ivyo vyatumye Hall n'abandi bahiganwa, harimwo abaserukira Sudani y'Epfo, bihutira kurondera uruhusha rwo kwinjira muri Amerika, ariko ntivyaboroheye.

Hall yagize ati: "Nk'uko vyari bitegekanijwe, uno musi ni wo nari nkwiye gufatirako urugendo rwerekeza muri Puerto Rico, aho nari kwitaba ihiganwa rya Miss Universe rigiye kuba ku ncuro ya 75."

Zimbabwe kiri mu bihugu 19 vyafatiwe ingingo zo kutemererwa canke kugabanirizwa ingendo zerekeza muri Amerika, hakurikijwe itangazo rya Perezida Trump nomero 10998, ryatanguye gukurikizwa ku wa 1 Nzero (1) 2026.

Izo ngingo zahagaritse itangwa ry'impusha zo kuja muri Amerika ku banyagihugu b'ivyo bihugu, baba abaja mu bukerarugendo canke mu ngendo z'ubudandaji, abanyeshure, abaja mu bikorwa vyo gusabikanya ubumenyi n'imico kama, hamwe n'abaja kuba muri Amerika. Harashizweho n'izindi nzitizi ku zindi mpusha zo kwinjira muri Amerika zitangwa ku bantu batagiye kuhaba.

Amakuru ya BBC Gahuza ako kanya kuri WhatsApp yawe

Mw'itangazo, ishirahamwe ritegura ihiganwa Miss Universe muri Zambia ryavuze ko ingorane Mubanga afise zatewe n'izo ngingo za Amerika, rishimangira ko atari ingorane ziwe bwite.

Iryo tangazo ryagize riti: "Bitandukanye n'igihe umwigeme ahiganwa yimwe uruhusha rwo kuja muri Amerika kubera ingorane ziwe bwite, impapuro adafise canke ingorane zijanye n'ishirahamwe rimurungitse, ikibazo ca Mubanga gifitaniye isano n'ingingo Perezida wa Amerika yafashe zo kubuza ingendo ziva muri Zambia no mu bindi bihugu vya Afrika."

Mubanga, afise imyaka 25 kandi akaba ari umuforomakazi, yatsindiye ikibanza co guhagararira Zambia muri Miss Universe ku wa 8 Gitugutu (10). Ni we vyitezwe ko azohagararira ico gihugu muri iryo higanwa mpuzamakungu.

Iryo tangazo ryavuze ko hari ibindi bihugu bitanu vyo muri Afrika vyahuye n'ingorane nk'izo, ariko ntiryabitomoye amazina.

Hall yavuze ko na we yumva ingorane abo bandi bahiganwa barimwo, yongerako ko yari amaze amayinga atari make ari muri Afrika y'Epfo, agerageza kuronka uruhusha rwo kuja muri Amerika.

Ati: "Si jewe gusa mfise iyi ngorane. Hari abandi bagenzanje bo muri Afrika bahuye n'ingorane nk'izi, kandi ndazi neza ivyo bariko baracamwo."

Uwuserukira Sudani y'Epfo muri Miss Universe na we nyene yagaragaje ko atazi neza nimba azoshobora kwitaba ihiganwa. Mu kwishura kuri videwo ya Hall, yanditse ati: "Miss Universe, amahirwe yo gushika muri Puerto Rico ni 50 kuri 50."

Mu yindi videwo yari yashize ku rubuga rwiwe hasigaye imisi itatu, Hall yavuze ko yari agifise icizere c'uko azoshobora gushika muri Puerto Rico.

Yanditse ayiherekeza ati: "Urugamba rwo gushikana Zimbabwe muri Puerto Rico rurabandanya."

Igice ca nyuma c'iryo higanwa gitegekanijwe kubera ku kibuga c'inkino ca José Miguel Agrelot Coliseum, mu gisagara ca San Juan.

MN202611_57quna522s.t:
Cambodian Prime Minister has expressed satisfaction of his county hosting the 20th edition of the la Francophonie summit describing it as source of pride.

“For our country, this is a moment of pride, a moment of unity, and a moment of celebration,” said Prime Minister Hun Manet on Nov 13.

Manet made the remarks during the official opening of the la Francophonie village ahead of the Summit.

He stressed the power of shared language and culture to unite nations and foster peace and prosperity.

He said that the La Francophonie village had become an open gateway to each summit.

In Cambodia, however, Manet said the village carries particular significance, reflecting the country’s identity as a place where rivers and cultures converge.

“Now, it is Phnom Penh’s turn to open this gateway as the village is situated in the heart of the capital, near the ‘Four Faces,’ or Chaktomuk River, the confluence where the rivers meet,” the prime minister said.

“Here, the waters have come together, just as the Mekong has always flowed, and here, too, the people converge. Cambodia and the Francophonie share a long history.”

According to Manet the French language spoken among bloc members has the ability to bridge nations and bring people together despite their differences.

The Cambodian prime minister noted that la Francophonie, “encompasses vibrant cultures. It is a space of opportunity, commerce, and innovation.”

He added that it is also a community grounded in values including peace, human dignity and solidarity.

Cambodia joined the Francophonie as an observer in 1991 before becoming a full member in 1993.

It becomes the second country in Southeast Asia to host the event, following Vietnam in 1997.

MN202611_dw6zk1zw0v.t:
What happened overnight with the Microsoft global outage?

At least 74 countries were affected by the Microsoft outage which was detected after midday US Eastern Time (17:00 GMT) on Thursday.

Microsoft 365 Services, including Teams, Outlook and artificial intelligence software Copilot, all experienced "connectivity problems", the company said.

As of early Friday afternoon (GMT), Microsoft was reporting improvements, with email queues "significantly reduced and approaching normal levels".

From city governments in the US to Australian spy agencies, the disruption was widespread. Here is what happened around the world.

In the US , staff with the House of Representatives told Politico , external their work had been halted by the outage.

"We all use Outlook, that's our life, everything is there, our calendar is there, our boss's calendar, so it has been a challenge … with no access to our Bible," one House staff member said. "There goes a day of legislative work."

Tech giants OpenAI and Anthropic both reported problems.

OpenAI, which makes ChatGPT, said it was investigating an issue affecting its connections to Microsoft's services, which caused some tools not to work as expected.

Courts from Los Angeles to Texas also warned that communications might be delayed.

Electric truck maker Workhorse Group, which was expected to report third-quarter results on 12 November, rescheduled to 16 November, citing business disruptions caused by the outage.

Meanwhile, officials in some US cities encouraged citizens to call local offices and agencies where needed instead of using email.

The City of Austin in Texas account posted on X early on Friday: "Due to an ongoing Microsoft Outlook outage, City of Austin employees cannot receive or send emails at this time.

"City phone lines remain operational, and 911 Emergency services are not impacted."

In Canada , a healthcare network running several hospitals in Toronto declared a "code grey", indicating an infrastructure failure.

The company, Unity Health Toronto, said its teams were having trouble sending or receiving email but that patient care was not affected.

Other hospitals, including Canada's largest children's hospital SickKids, also reported its staff having issues accessing phone calls and emails.

Via Rail, Canada's national train network, said in a post on X that its passengers might not be able to receive emails about their trips because of the outage.

Disruptions were also reported by Canadian municipalities, including the City of Ottawa and the City of Vancouver. Both urged residents in a notice to call in for any urgent issues.

Schools, GPs and businesses hit by global Microsoft outage as company scrambles to solve issue

What we know about the global Microsoft outage

In Japan , some companies reportedly turned to fax machines to maintain communications.

"Can't send emails because of a Microsoft outage, so we're switching to fax for the regular updates we usually send as PDFs. Analog is strong," one unnamed X user was quoted as saying by the Japan Times , external .

The Japanese government said its shared IT platform had been disrupted.

"We understand that Microsoft is working to restore services, and we will continue to monitor the company's response," Deputy Chief Cabinet Secretary Masanao Ozaki told reporters.

Singapore also confirmed the outage had affected some government systems, but stressed "emergency services remain fully operational".

Singapore's courts also said they were "experiencing issues with incoming and outgoing emails", urging people to contact them by telephone for urgent matters.

In the Philippines , the Supreme Court warned that "responses to emails and other transactions may be delayed".

In India , the outage was disrupting work for many on Friday, with emails not landing and Teams calls not going through smoothly.

People working in the equity markets told BBC News they had panicked when they realised they could not access daily research reports before their morning meeting where they make their big decisions of the day.

"Outlook wasn't working. We fortunately have an alternative so it was not a problem. But we conduct most of our calls, especially with big clients, on Teams - that has been a challenge," a senior executive with a big Indian brokerage said on condition of anonymity.

Firms in China use software that has been made locally - WPS Office is a favourite - but the Microsoft outage caused frustration there too.

Outlook is one of the few reliable channels for many offices and businesses in the country who work with colleagues across the world.

China operates one of the world's most sophisticated systems of internet censorship, known as the Great Firewall, which restricts access to many Western websites including Google, Facebook and Instagram along with many international news organisations including the BBC.

Australia's spy and federal police agencies were affected by the outage, though officials suggested the impact was minimal.

"The impact that they are dealing with is very much on email system," the head of the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation, Mike Burgess, told reporters.

Other Australian public service providers also confirmed they had been affected by the outage, but similarly said this was mostly limited to emails, and the BBC understands there were no major impacts across New South Wales' primary services in health, education, transport, and emergency services.

European stock market operator Euronext advised listed companies on Friday morning to use the phone to communicate corporate information because of the Outlook email disruption, Reuters reported.

Speaking to the same news agency, the head of Germany 's BSI cybersecurity agency, Claudia Plattner, said the country's authorities had not been affected because they did not rely on Microsoft 365 services.

However, Reuters reported that Germany's national rail operator, Deutsche Bahn, was having difficulties sending out timetables for diverted trains due to the outage.

Plattner added the disruption was "affecting the whole world". "It is a global disruption that spans a vast number of data centres – stretching from Asia right across to the US, via Europe," she said.

In Antalya, Turkey , advisers and officials attending the UN Climate Change Conference, Cop31, were left frustrated by the outage.

James Young, a climate change adviser at the Inuit Circumpolar Council, the organisation which represents around 180,000 Inuit people living in the Arctic, told Reuters the council relied on emails and Microsoft Teams to communicate across several countries.

"It's just been really frustrating and challenging to maintain contact with our colleagues and to be able to effectively participate here," he said. "I think our dependence on technology leaves us vulnerable to situations like this."

In the UK , GPs, police and pharmacies were among services affected.

Some GP surgeries have urged patients not to submit messages via their website while the problem remains, while several large police forces are urging members of the public to call if they want to make a report.

Politicians are also affected. At Westminster, MPs were reporting their access via parliamentary accounts to Microsoft products was down.

A parliamentary spokesperson said: "We are aware of the global issue affecting Microsoft email services, which is impacting users of the parliamentary network. We are working with Microsoft to resolve the matter as quickly as possible.

"Alternative communication arrangements are in place, allowing today's business to continue."

Some parts of Asia, Europe and Africa were unaffected, according to Downdetector. These include Russia, where the use of Microsoft applications is heavily restricted, or phased out in favour of domestic alternatives.

However, this could also be a case of under-reporting in some countries, where Downdetector is among the websites blocked due to censorship.

One winemaker in South Africa said almost his entire business had been brought to a "standstill" by the Microsoft outage.

"It's incredibly frustrating," Peter Pentz added. "We export a lot, so communication with exporters in Europe has come to a standstill."

Order processing, dispatch, communications and even "critical production work" were halted, he said, as the Cape West Coast winery "relies on these systems for parts of our day-to-day operations".

Leicester City will travel to Crabble, the home of Dover Athletic of National League South

Non-league clubs Dover Athletic and Salisbury will stage the BBC's two chosen FA Cup second-round ties next month.

National League South side Dover welcome former Premier League and FA Cup winners Leicester City to Crabble on Saturday, 5 December (17:15 GMT, BBC Two/iPlayer).

Another sixth-tier side, Salisbury, will host Blackpool, winners of one of the most memorable finals of all time in 1953, at the Raymond McEnhill Stadium the following day (Sunday 6 December, 12:15 GMT, BBC Two/iPlayer).

Dover reached the second round courtesy of a 2-0 home win over National League side Wealdstone and are seeking to reach round three for just the third time in their history, having lost against Huddersfield in 2011 and at home to Premier League outfit Crystal Palace in 2015.

The Foxes - who lost on their first four FA Cup final appearances before Youri Tielemans' goal secured a 1-0 win over Chelsea in the 2021 final - now play in League One after back-to-back relegations and overcame Oxford City of National League North 4-2 in the first round.

Salisbury are yet to concede a goal in their three ties this season and thrashed Sholing 6-0 to reach round two for the first time since the club was reformed in 2015.

Seventh-tier sides Wimborne Town and Plymouth Parkway will also see their home ties against League One Bradford City and League Two Barnet, respectively, televised among the eight selected for live coverage across the weekend.

All clubs featured in live television broadcasts will receive £60,000 while the winning and losing clubs in the second round will receive £79,500 and £21,200 respectively from the competition prize fund.

The third round draw will take place before the televised tie between Guiseley and Notts County at 19:30 GMT on Monday, 7 December.

A comprehensive highlights programme will cover the weekend's action on Sunday, 6 December at 17:10 GMT (BBC Two/iPlayer).

All of the second round's goals will be available to view across BBC digital platforms including the BBC Sport website and app.

MN202611_1p8c0k6la2c.t:
La Francophonie is scheduled to hold it’s 48th edition of the Ministerial Conference at the Sokha Phnom Penh Hotel / Chroy Changvar International Convention and Exhibition Centre.

This Ministerial Conference on November 14 will bring together foreign ministers and government representatives from the International Organisation of La Francophonie’s (OIF) member states, governments, and observers.

According to organisers, the Ministerial Conference is a platform for preparing matters and formulating recommendations for the heads of state and government attending the upcoming 20th Francophonie Summit.

The conference deliberations will largely focus on “Reinvesting in Peace for Shared Prosperity and Sustainable Stability”.

In preparation for key documents Ministers will tomorrow finalise core texts for summit adoption, including the Phnom Penh Declaration, a resolution on peacebuilding and crisis resolution, and the Phnom Penh Appeal for cultural heritage and diversity.

What about candidates for the organisation’s secretary General slot?

The Ministerial conference will feature candidate presentations and closed-door deliberations for the election of the OIF Secretary-General, alongside reviews of institutional and financial governance.

As member states of la Francophonie seek to intergrade technology, ministers at the conference tomorrow will seek to coordinate economic initiatives, supporting parallel gatherings such as FrancoTech 2026 (covering AI, digital governance, fintech, and food security) and the Francophone Entrepreneurs Forum.

MN202611_12l18fku4we.t:
The Francophonie bloc of nearly 396 million people, half of this population are youth. Over 50% of the Francophone population is under the age of 35.

At the Francophonie Pavilion, young people from Réseau international de la jeunesse de la Francophonie RIJF and PFJ presented to the Secretary General 10 recommendations from the Lomé consultation, calling for a Francophonie that is more attentive to the aspirations and ambitions of its youth.

Around 30 young delegates gathered to draft recommendations and priorities for the 20th Francophone Summit in Phnom Penh, Cambodia.

The Francophonie youth met OIF Sec.Gen. Louis Mushikiwabo and expressed their support to her third term bid.

“Francophonie young people, express our deep gratitude to Mushikiwabo for her constant attention she pays to young people, recognizing and valuing their role within our Organization for eight years,” said one the the youths at the summit.

“To consolidate our achievements and build on the progress made, we are convinced that her continued leadership of the Francophonie remains essential.”

Mushikiwabo invited the Francophone community to make the most of the activities and gatherings on offer at the Village.

She said that beyond its political dimension, the Summit is also a time for sharing that brings people closer together.

MN202611_12gb7tfx181.t:
PHNOM PENH — President Paul Kagame and First Lady Jeannette Kagame were officially received with full state honours by King Norodom Sihamoni at the Royal Palace in Phnom Penh on Friday, November 13, marking a historic milestone in bilateral relations between Rwanda and the Kingdom of Cambodia.

The royal reception formally launched President Kagame’s first-ever State Visit to the Southeast Asian nation, undertaken at the invitation of King Sihamoni ahead of the 20th Summit of the International Organisation of La Francophonie (OIF).

Upon their arrival at the Royal Palace on Friday morning, the Rwandan Head of State and the First Lady were greeted by King Sihamoni in an official welcoming ceremony held in front of the Tevea Vinichhay Throne Hall.

Following the ceremonial honours, King Sihamoni granted President Kagame and First Lady Jeannette Kagame a private royal audience inside the palace.

Earlier in the day, President Kagame and the First Lady paid solemn tribute to Cambodia’s national heritage and history, laying wreaths at the Independence Monument and at the Royal Memorial Statue of the late King-Father Norodom Sihanouk in central Phnom Penh.

The state visit began on Thursday afternoon, November 12, when the Rwandan presidential delegation landed at Cambodia’s Techo International Airport in Kandal province.

They were welcomed on the tarmac by a high-level Cambodian delegation led by Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of the Royal Palace Kuy Sophal, alongside Minister of Inspection Sok Soken, who was specially assigned by Prime Minister Hun Manet to oversee the government’s reception.

Following Friday morning’s royal engagements, President Kagame transitioned to high-level political and economic talks at the Senate’s Solidarity Palace, where he held a courtesy call and bilateral discussions with Senate President Samdech Techo Hun Sen.

During the talks, Hun Sen noted that Cambodia and Rwanda share similar stages of national development, creating strong opportunities for both countries to exchange experiences and learn from one another.

President Kagame affirmed that his delegation is actively looking to deepen and expand cooperation across key sectors.

President Kagame’s bilateral itinerary also includes separate meetings with National Assembly President Khuon Sudary and Prime Minister Hun Manet.

According to Cambodia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, the engagements are set to culminate in the signing of bilateral cooperation agreements spanning four priority areas: trade, investment, civil aviation, and tourism.

The agreements build upon diplomatic relations formally established between Kigali and Phnom Penh in 2005.

Following the conclusion of his bilateral state visit, President Kagame will join heads of state and government from across the Francophone world in Phnom Penh from November 15 to 16 for the 20th Francophonie Summit, convened under the theme “Reinvesting in peace for shared prosperity and lasting stability.”

MN202611_g0ocvtkc9j.t:
Ezekiel Williams was a "box-to-box midfielder with high energy who was not afraid of a tackle", says Hendon chairman Cyrus Cooper

"I messaged Ezekiel because we had a midweek cup game and I wanted to check he was still available," says Adam Fisher - manager of non-league Hendon.

"There was no reply. Then I found out what had happened."

Ezekiel Williams died in hospital on 2 November from head injuries after an incident in Milton Keynes. He was 26.

Known to friends as 'Zekes' and 'Eze', Williams was well known in non-league circles having played for clubs including Hastings United, Kettering Town and St Ives Town.

A midfielder, he joined Hendon in September and had already established himself at his new club as a "humble, unassuming and generous individual with razor-sharp wit".

His death has devastated the part-time club based in Kingsbury, north-west London.

"Nothing prepares you for something like this," Hendon's chairman Cyrus Cooper tells BBC Sport. "We're all human beings and the club is struggling to come to terms with what has happened."

Hendon, who play in the Isthmian League South Central Division - the eighth tier of English football, have not played since Williams died, as players and staff mourn the loss of a popular player.

On Saturday, 12 days after his death, they return to action at Bedfont Sports.

"Saturday is going to be so hard because Eze is going to be on our minds and what happened to him," Hendon midfielder Tashae Andall-Gibbons tells BBC Sport.

"Everyone is distraught. Eze was only 26 and had his whole life ahead of him."

Cooper says: "It's going to be the first time the players put their kit on without Ezekiel being there.

"I think there are going to be a lot of tears. It's going to be an emotional day for everyone associated with Hendon Football Club."

Ezekiel Williams (right) with his brother Omran and sister Shadore

Hendon's grieving players have been offered counselling as they attempt to come to terms with the loss of a team-mate who scored in a league game against Jersey Bulls as recently as 24 October.

Three days later, Williams - from Ruislip - started the 2-0 home defeat by Egham Town.

"He messaged me the day after to say: 'Gaffer, I'm really sorry I didn't catch you after the game but I'm going away for the weekend to see a relative who is sick'," says Fisher.

"He said: 'I won't be at training on Thursday, I will miss the game on Saturday but I'll be back on Monday.'

Fisher sent Williams a message on the Monday asking about his availability for a London Cup tie against Woodford, which was due to take place a couple of days later.

There was no reply. The following day, via social media, he discovered his player had died.

"I found out on the Tuesday afternoon and I didn't leave my house until the Friday," he says. "I was shocked and in a daze."

As manager of Welwyn Garden City for seven years, Fisher has delivered hundreds of team talks.

He has thought long and hard about the one he will give to his grief-stricken players on Saturday.

"What can you say that the players are going to take in?" says Fisher, who has watched interviews with Liverpool players about the impact Diogo Jota's death had on them, in an attempt to learn more about how to deal with grief inside a dressing room.

"I've got a squad of players who are mourning the loss of one of their team-mates. We are all really struggling."

Cooper adds: "Ezekiel was very courteous and softly spoken. I remember we lost a match and he came up to me after the game and apologised. That was the type of man he was."

Hendon's players say a prayer for Williams at training on Thursday

Away from Hendon, Williams coached children at football coaching company JOAP (Journey Of A Pro).

"I've had lots of messages from parents saying how much Zekes made their kids feel so special," says Tyrique Clarke - CEO and head of coaching at JOAP, and Williams' best friend.

"We met about 14 years ago and we spoke every day about everything.

"He was a real source of comfort for me. Someone I would speak to about every decision. Who do I ask now? He was just the most selfless, loving person and always a bright spark of energy."

Clarke adds: "Zekes loved coaching children. He would always give them a little Bible quote or motivational speech in team talks before games. He was just a genuine, kind-hearted person."

A crowdfunding page set up in Williams' memory has raised nearly £19,000.

Players and staff at Hendon have contributed, and the club will pay tribute to Williams at their next home game against Ascot United on 28 November.

Williams attended church and would send his group of friends a meaningful Bible verse every day

Williams' sister Shadore paid tribute to her brother.

"Seeing Ezekiel get older and gain different ambitions in life was the best thing I could have witnessed," she said. , external

"He got to become a football coach and teach children who loved the same sport as he did.

"He became closer to God and said he wanted to attend church and would get excited each time he got a new suit and would show it off to the family."

On Thursday, Hendon's players met up for training to try to prepare for Saturday's game.

The chairman attended to give a speech after a traumatic week for the club, while Hendon's players said a prayer for their team-mate.

"Everybody is still trying to process what has happened," adds Andall-Gibbons. "I hope we use this pain in the right way and put on a big performance on Saturday.

If you have been affected by issues raised in this article, there is information and support available on BBC Action Line.

MN202611_qumkj0ehxm.t:
Bruno Fernandes joined Manchester United from Sporting in 2020

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has rejected a second contract offer from the club.

The Portugal midfielder is out of contract at the end of the season, though the club have the option to trigger a 12-month extension until 2028.

United are keen to avoid that eventuality by extending the 32-year-old's existing deal and have been in talks with the Portuguese's representatives in recent months.

But sources have told BBC Sport that Fernandes has rejected the club's second proposal over a new deal at Old Trafford.

Should United fail to agree a fresh deal with Fernandes, it is almost certain that the club will trigger a 12-month extension in his contract before 1 January.

How Ferguson-inspired Pochettino can succeed where Carrick failed at Man Utd

At that point, the midfielder would be able to sign a pre-contract agreement with foreign clubs as his contract would be within six months of expiring.

It is unclear when Fernandes turned down the offer, but it appears unlikely that a resolution is imminent given the upheaval at the club.

Michael Carrick was sacked as head coach on Thursday following the club's worst start to a domestic campaign in 40 years.

USA coach Mauricio Pochettino is expected to replace Carrick, with the Argentine set to be in charge for the first time when United travel to Anfield to face rivals Liverpool on 22 November.

United will be hoping that Pochettino's arrival will persuade Fernandes to commit his future to the club.

Fernandes came close to joining Pochettino's Tottenham in 2019 but a move failed to materialise, with the midfielder signing for United six months later.

The former Sporting midfielder has scored six times in 13 matches for United this season.

In theory, the current contract stand-off between Manchester United and Bruno Fernandes is not a big deal.

It is usual for the first, second and sometimes quite a few more offers to be rejected as part of the rough and tumble of negotiations.

United do have the option to trigger an option to add an extra year. However, there is reason why both sides might be wary to commit beyond that at this stage.

On Fernandes' part, there is a clear desire to compete for the biggest prizes. He can see the best years of his career drifting away. Yet again United have failed to build on a season of promise and he will now be wanting to see what impact Mauricio Pochettino has when he eventually arrives from the United States.

Fernandes was coveted by the Saudi Pro League 18 months ago, although the feeling has been he would prefer to stay in Europe.

On United's side, they will have noted Fernandes' alarming drop-off from the levels he hit last season, when he broke the Premier League assists record and won all the major player of the year honours.

Liverpool committed a huge amount of money to Mohamed Salah's last contract and that turned out to be a heavy financial burden. United will not want to get saddled with a major contract over an extended period for an underperforming player.

MN202611_1koyzgjz2u9.t:
Beneath the ceremonial traditions of Cambodia’s Royal Palace, President Paul Kagame and First Lady Jeannette Kagame received a royal welcome from King Norodom Sihamoni on Friday, November 13, marking a significant moment in Rwanda’s diplomatic engagement with the Southeast Asian nation.

The reception, held in Cambodia’s capital, Phnom Penh, was more than a formal gesture of hospitality.

It represented an opportunity for two countries separated by thousands of kilometres to strengthen relations and explore new avenues of cooperation in an increasingly interconnected world.

For President Kagame, the royal audience marked a central moment in his state visit to Cambodia, which began on Thursday, November 12, at the invitation of King Norodom Sihamoni.

The Cambodian monarch received the Rwandan leader and the First Lady at the Royal Palace, where the two sides also held private discussions.

The visit comes at a time when Rwanda is seeking to deepen its international partnerships beyond its traditional diplomatic and economic relationships, while Cambodia is looking to expand cooperation with African countries.

Despite their geographical distance, Rwanda and Cambodia share an interest in developing stronger economic partnerships, attracting investment and expanding international cooperation.

Turning diplomatic relations into economic opportunities

One of the central objectives of Kagame’s visit is to translate longstanding diplomatic relations into practical opportunities for businesses and institutions in both countries.

The two nations established diplomatic relations in 2005, but their engagement has increasingly focused on identifying areas where closer cooperation could deliver economic benefits.

During the visit, Kagame is expected to hold separate meetings with Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet, Senate President Hun Sen and National Assembly President Khuon Sudary.

Discussions are expected to focus on strengthening bilateral relations, with particular attention to trade, investment, aviation and tourism.

Several agreements and cooperation documents are also expected to be signed, potentially creating new frameworks for economic and business engagement.

These areas are particularly important for Rwanda, which continues to position itself as a regional investment, tourism and aviation hub, while seeking partnerships that can open new markets for its businesses.

The visit builds on progress made in November 2025, when Cambodian Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn visited Rwanda.

During that engagement, the two countries signed agreements establishing regular consultations between their foreign ministries and removing visa requirements for holders of diplomatic and official passports.

The latest engagement therefore offers an opportunity to build on those diplomatic foundations and move towards broader economic cooperation.

From the Royal Palace to the global Francophone stage

Beyond bilateral relations, Kagame’s presence in Phnom Penh also places Rwanda at the centre of an important international diplomatic gathering.

Cambodia is preparing to host the 20th Summit of the International Organisation of La Francophonie (OIF) on November 15 and 16, bringing together leaders of French-speaking countries and governments from different regions of the world.

The summit will be held under the theme, “Reinvest in Peace for Shared Prosperity and Lasting Stability.”

For Rwanda, the gathering carries additional significance because its candidate, Louise Mushikiwabo, is seeking a third term as Secretary-General of the organisation, a position she has held since 2018.

The leadership contest is expected to attract considerable diplomatic attention, particularly as candidates from other countries seek to take over the organisation’s leadership for the 2027–2030 term.

Cambodia’s hosting of the summit also represents an important moment for Southeast Asia, as it provides a platform for strengthening connections between Asian and African countries through the Francophone community.

For Kagame and the First Lady, the royal reception offers a symbolic beginning to a visit whose importance extends beyond diplomatic protocol.

As Rwanda and Cambodia explore cooperation in aviation, tourism, trade and investment, the broader question is how the goodwill expressed through high-level engagements can translate into tangible opportunities for their citizens and businesses.

The coming meetings and agreements will provide an indication of how far the two countries are prepared to take that relationship.

In Phnom Penh, the royal welcome has opened another chapter in Rwanda’s engagement with Southeast Asia, bringing two countries with different histories and geographical realities closer through shared diplomatic and economic interests.

MN202611_m21py4n5tm.t:
The Francophonie Village opened in Phnom Penh on Friday, November 13, launching five days of cultural events alongside Cambodia’s hosting of the 20th Francophonie Summit.

Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet and Louise Mushikiwabo, Secretary-General of the International Organisation of La Francophonie (OIF), attended the opening ceremony.

Set up at Wat Botum Park, the village is open to the public and brings together national pavilions, exhibitions, cultural performances, discussions and food from across the Francophone world.

Its programme is designed to showcase the community’s cultural diversity and encourage exchanges among its members.

Rwanda is represented at the gathering by President Paul Kagame, who is in Cambodia for a state visit and to attend the summit. His visit is also an opportunity to discuss stronger bilateral relations and cooperation with Cambodian leaders.

The summit is especially significant for Rwanda because Mushikiwabo, a Rwandan, is seeking a third term as OIF Secretary-General.

Member states are due to choose the organisation’s next leader during the summit, scheduled for November 15 and 16.

The Francophonie Village will remain open until November 17, extending the summit’s focus beyond diplomatic meetings and giving visitors a chance to experience the cultures, traditions and ideas of Francophone countries.

MN202611_zb4wzbb6c5.t:
Rwanda’s President Paul Kagame has paid tribute to the founding father of the Cambodian State.

“Earlier today in Phnom Penh, President Kagame and First Lady Jeannette Kagame visited the Independence Monument and the monument honouring His Majesty Preah Bat Samdech Preah Norodom Sihanouk, the late King-Father of Cambodia, “Preah Borom Ratanak Kaudh,” the Rwanda Presidency said.

The Rwandan leader and First Lady Jeannette Kagame honoured the late King-Father by laying a wreath at his memorial monument during a visit to Phnom Penh.

Preah Borom Ratanak Kaudh is the posthumous title of His Majesty Preah Bat Samdech Preah Norodom Sihanouk, the late King-Father of Cambodia (October 31, 1922 – October 15, 2012).

He was a major figure in securing Cambodia’s complete independence from France on November 9, 1953.

MN202611_1kedqqv6n7p.t:
Key services across the UK, including the NHS, GPs and schools, have been affected by a global Microsoft outage.

Pharmacies and businesses have also been hit after email and messaging services went down.

NHS England said patients should still attend appointments unless told otherwise, while several large police forces are urging the public to call if they want to report a crime.

Microsoft said services were now gradually being restored globally after a problem caused by a higher-than-usual stress on its servers, but users could still experience disruption.

The government said it was working closely with the firm to assess any impact on its services, while local authorities warned that some council services were being affected.

The full extent of the impact of the outage - which is affecting Outlook, Teams and Copilot - and the time it will take to restore the systems remains unclear hours after users first reported issues.

Some 430 million people use the online tools worldwide.

The chief executive of the NHS Alliance, which represents the healthcare system in England, Wales and Northern Ireland, said the outage was affecting some services including emails.

NHS trusts in England were enacting measures to minimise disruption to critical services, a spokesperson said.

Patients have been told to continue to use 999 in an emergency and otherwise contact 111 by phone or online, or their local pharmacy.

Some GP surgeries have urged patients not to submit messages via their website while the problem remains. Practices in Hampshire and Shropshire have told patients to phone them or come into the surgery if they have an urgent need.

Microsoft scrambles to solve global outage affecting Outlook and Teams but says fixes not going 'as expected'

What we know about the global Microsoft outage

A National Pharmacy Association spokesperson said the outage was affecting pharmacies' ability to communicate with GP practices and some patients, so "waits may be longer than normal and there may be delays to some prescriptions".

The overall impact on health services remains unclear. Much of the NHS calendar is linked to diaries using the Microsoft system, but workflow practices differ between hospitals and trusts.

There are anecdotal reports of c-sections being cancelled and hospitals only accepting urgent referrals - though the impact on elective treatments has yet to be confirmed.

The GMB union's national secretary Rachel Harrison said the outage was having a "serious impact" on ambulance and NHS trusts.

"Those who work in 111 and 999 services are unable to refer patient details in the normal way which is creating a massive backlog and has the potential for chaos," she said, though "emergency and life-threatening call outs appear to be unaffected".

Meanwhile, police forces in England and Wales - including the Metropolitan Police, Greater Manchester Police and Police Scotland - have said online forms may be affected. They are urging people to call them about any time-critical by non-emergency matters.

Downing Street said it was looking to get a "full picture" of the the extent of the outage's effect on government services.

In England, the Local Government Association warned that some services may be disrupted but plans were in place to ensure people "continue to receive the support they need".

Because the outage affects key organisational and communication platforms that are integrated, many other workplaces have been affected.

That has included schools, where teachers, office staff and parents have all had to navigate being unable to access key resources on calendars, emails and internal cloud servers.

One head teacher at a primary school near Newcastle said safeguarding systems had also been affected, meaning staff were having to report concerns in person instead of logging them, while another in Cheshire said his had been forced to delay sending out termly school reports.

Universities have also suffered disruption to online systems, including tools used to submit assignments.

Some, like the University of Portsmouth and University of Aberdeen, have extended deadlines or waived late submission penalties.

Royal Mail said some of its online services were unavailable and email notifications about deliveries may be impacted, but post was still being collected and delivered as normal

MPs have been unable to access their parliamentary accounts. A spokesperson said alternative arrangements were in place

The Scottish government has activated its "resilience operations" as it assesses the impact of the outage

MSPs also confirmed that Holyrood's emails systems were down, meaning they were unable to communicate with constituents or access urgent casework

Some businesses are reverting to using paper or moving to different communication platforms like WhatsApp.

Microsoft and cyber-security experts have ruled out a cyber-attack being the cause of the outage.

The tech firm said a large number of its servers had become "unexpectedly unavailable", meaning traffic was sent to the servers that remained online, putting them under strain.

"Just like on a motorway, when you block one lane, you have to put all of the excess traffic through just, say, one or two lanes," Jake Moore, a cyber-security adviser at ESET, explained.

"Everything goes and backs up. It slows down, and that's what we're seeing here."

He told BBC Radio 4's Today programme that this incident should "hammer home" the need for contingency communication networks that are "independent of others".

"Unfortunately, we just put so much emphasis on just a few providers - so when one big one like this goes down, the knock-on effects are just huge."

His sentiment was echoed by Nicky Choo, who said his cyber-security firm Mimecast used Microsoft tools but had built-in alternatives to prevent disruption.

Some workplaces are reverting to using paper or moving to alternate communication platforms like WhatsApp to keep their businesses ticking over.

But others have been left struggling without the Microsoft tools.

Caroline Wade, who runs her own PR agency in Kent, told the BBC that the outage had caused her "huge disruption" as she was unable to send pitches and invoices.

Meanwhile, 29-year-old Georgia Young, from Staffordshire, was due to complete a house purchase today with her partner but said it had now been delayed.

"We've waited eight months to get to this point, it seem like it's out of reach again," she said.

Dave Walker said the outage was threatening his fledgling bakery and wine bar's online pre-Christmas sales, while Stirlingshire resident Lewis Bowles said he was unable to access his tickets for a Sunday rugby match.

MN202611_1j9s3t2l09w.t:
Installing a heat pump is a big decision

Floorplans. Air duct diagrams. Heat pump specifications. Most people in the market for a new heating system probably don't want to think about this level of detail.

But, perhaps surprisingly, some do want to think about those things. In extreme depth.

Every day, roughly 150 new users sign up to an app called Cool Calc, which works out the heat requirements of properties in the US.

Just over one third of those new users are not tradespeople but private homeowners, says founder and chief executive Bill Fiore.

When choosing a heating system, people can find themselves bombarded with information – how powerful a heat pump do they need, for example? It isn't always easy to take a tradesperson at their word.

"As an overall trend, we are seeing homeowners be more informed," explains Fiore. "They want to do a calculation on their own."

Cool Calc is used by tradespeople and homeowners to work out heat loss

A heat loss calculation is a figure, usually measured in watts, that defines how much heat a home loses during cold weather. It's worked out room by room and is a key part of designing an efficient heating system.

This estimate is especially important to get right when installing a heat pump, which is sized fairly precisely, according to the projected heat loss.

Should that calculation be off, the heat pump will likely perform poorly. You could be left with an underpowered device that struggles to warm your property, for example. Given the costs involved, homeowners are often anxious to ensure installers avoid such mistakes.

Certain new technologies are not, for the moment, helping, adds Fiore. "People are going to AI and they're getting a lot of misinformation because it's not backed by anything credible," he says. Cool Calc is planning to integrate with AI chatbots to try and improve the quality of the advice they spew out.

It is probably a good idea to be cautious about your new heating system's design, says Kevin Kircher at Purdue University. He and colleagues recently conducted a study, yet to be published, examining the heat loss calculations provided by tradespeople to roughly 75 US homeowners.

"We were surprised," says Kircher. "The heat loss calculations often led to overestimating the design heat loads by a factor of two or more." That would result in oversized systems that use much more power than necessary.

Not only that, some people reported charges of more than $1,000 (£745) – and in one case as much as $2,500 – just for a heat loss survey, adds Kircher.

Besides using excessive amounts of energy, an oversized heating system can also feel uncomfortable, says Dan Dempsey, a former senior engineering fellow for a major heating and cooling provider in the US.

Dempsey, who took part in Kircher and his colleagues' study, lives in Indiana. He says it is his retirement hobby to monitor the performance of heating and cooling systems in the homes of friends and family members, by analysing data from their smart thermostats.

"I spent five years manually downloading everything, every week," he says. He points out that oversized systems tend to cycle a lot, meaning they switch on and off again in quick succession.

This leads to discernible swings in temperature: rooms that fail to remain at their target temperature of, say, 20C, but rather fluctuate, which feels uncomfortable, says Dempsey.

For people seeking a better understanding of their home's heat loss, various free or partially free apps, including Cool Calc and AutoHVAC, are available. There are options for UK homeowners, too, such as web app Heatpunk.

Heat loss apps help drive business to renewable energy firms says Andy Rankin

Many things can influence the heat loss figure, including the amount of insulation in your home, whether the building has double or triple glazing, and also the size of your radiators.

Heatpunk allows people to draw a floor plan of their home and input data about the property in order to estimate its performance. Thousands of people use it every month, mostly professional installers, says Andy Rankin, founder and managing director of Midsummer Energy.

The web app also suggests specific heat pump models for each property, based on the results of the calculation. Naturally, these are models available through Midsummer Energy. "It's been a very effective marketing tool," says Rankin.

Dwellow, another company that offers heat pump installations in the UK, is keen to follow suit. The firm recently launched its own heat loss estimator.

While professional heat loss calculations remain essential, getting people to do their own "self surveys" first could ultimately reduce how much time professional heating engineers must spend analysing properties says Ian Mclaren, Dwellow's co-founder and director.

"Going into a home and just being able to check the information rather than start from scratch could turn a survey into a half-hour trip – far more efficient and less costly," says Mclaren.

There's no substitute for engineers doing a good job when it is their turn, however, stresses Maurizio Sibilla, of the Centre for Advanced Built Environment Research at the University of West England, Bristol.

"The solution is better installer practice, clearer customer-facing evidence, and improved methods, not expecting homeowners to do the engineering themselves," he says, adding that providing homeowners with information about the calculation and also data on heat pump performance post-installation can reassure them that the system works as expected.

Adam Chapman questions whether homeowners should do their own heat loss survey

Doing your own heat loss calculation may end up "over-intellectualising" things, says Adam Chapman, chief geek at heat pump training firm and installer network Heat Geek.

"I don't personally see what a homeowner would gain from it," he says. "We will guarantee the efficiency with way less radiators and pipework upgrades than any other system out there."

Chapman points out that only the most careful of surveys will capture a home's heat loss well.

He says it is common for Heat Geek installers to discover retrofitted windows that haven't been foam-insulated into their openings, leaving draughty gaps, or cavity walls that a homeowner thought had been insulated – but which were actually missed by the builder.

"It's stuff you can't see," he says. "What we actually need is home surveys that go and spot for these sorts of things."

The international criminal court (ICC) on Wednesday cancelled an arrest warrant that had been issued for FDLR’s top terrorist Sylvester Mudacumura.

According to emerging details, the ICC’s Pre-trial Chamber I on 12 November 2026 terminated proceedings against Mudacumura.

The decision to drop arrest of Mudacumura was based on his death as the Registry and the Prosecution provided.

“There is no indication that Mr Mudacumura is still alive,” the ICC said.

ICC added, “around 17 September 2019, Mudacumura was eliminated in a sting operation by Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (FARDC).

Therefore the chamber granted the Prosecution’s request to withdraw the Warrant of Arrest and terminated the proceedings against Mudacumura.

“Accordingly, any outstanding requests for cooperation related to these proceedings are no longer in effect,” the Court Said.

“Following the notification of his passing. According to the ICC legal framework, the Court’s jurisdiction cannot be exercised over a deceased person”.

Mudacumura, a former Supreme Commander of the Forces Démocratiques pour la Libération du Rwanda (FDLR) was issued on 13 July 2012, for 9 counts of war crimes.

The crimes were committed from 20 January 2009 to the end of September 2010; attacking civilians, murder, mutilation, cruel treatment, rape, torture, destruction of property, pillaging and outrages against personal dignity.

MN202611_15zzkb9rhpv.t:
Maurucio Pochettino (right) was first mentioned as a contender to manage Manchester United when Louis van Gaal was sacked in May 2016

When Mauricio Pochettino was asked the three Premier League managers he would have loved to have played for, he was unequivocal.

"Sir Alex Ferguson, Sir Alex Ferguson, Sir Alex Ferguson," replied Pochettino, who on Friday was named Manchester United manager.

In 2023, the Argentine - then at Chelsea , and dressed in full Blues training gear - was being interviewed by Sky Sports. Still he felt a need to express his adoration for Ferguson.

Six years prior to that interview, while managing Tottenham , he had shared lunch with the legendary former United manager.

"When I was young, when I started my career as a manager, he was always my inspiration, my reference," Pochettino said.

"And when you can share two hours with a person who was the greatest manager in the history of football, you can only enjoy."

Hiring United managers has been complicated since Ferguson's departure in 2013, and one of the most prominent complications has been a back-and-forth around the club's DNA.

For some, winning by any means necessary should take precedence, while others believe the style of play and cultural heritage of United's most successful period is vital to the club's identity.

In recent years, United's managerial merry-go-round has alternated between European coaches with their own fixed styles of play, and former players from the Ferguson era.

But between his tactics of choice and his adoration for the former United boss, Pochettino may be uniquely placed to bridge the gap between both camps.

Pochettino a decade in Man Utd's making - but Carrick deserves better

Michael Carrick's United produced a series of good results to finish last season with a run unmatched by any other team in the league. They looked great, but it was a greatness built on attacking in a transition-heavy manner.

Under Carrick, in games they had less than 50% of the ball, they only lost once. In those 13 games, they boasted a win-rate of 62%. This dropped to 36% in games they had the majority of possession.

This style of play suited their direct attackers and protected their defenders.

At the same time, Casemiro's set-piece prowess provided United a reliable way to break the deadlock against deep defences - something they have struggled with this season.

With United a goal up, opponents stepped forward, giving Carrick's men more space. They could play to their strengths again, attacking quickly. It worked.

But teams at the top are reluctant to play in this way. Carrick's vision for United was a side that played slick football, with short passes in build-up intuitively, referencing Paris St-Germain's midfield three as a source of inspiration.

Building up in this manner, to entice and escape from pressure, before looking to find the forwards quickly, was the plan Carrick was working towards.

This didn't come to fruition and trying to take United from a successful counter-attacking side to one that could reliably beat teams while keeping the ball was the same hurdle that undid Ole Gunnar Solskjar and Erik ten Hag.

Former players under Sir Alex Ferguson, both Ole Gunnar Solskjar and Michael Carrick leaned into United’s historic style when crafting their game-models

Pochettino gives United an interesting solution to this problem.

In his own words, he has described his sides as needing "to be protagonists, always press high, work hard and be dynamic". He refers to himself as a "disciple" of the legendary Argentina boss Marcelo Bielsa, who he played for.

If you wanted an immediate comparison in the Premier League to a coach who resembles Pochettino's ideas in possession, it would be worth looking at Liverpool 's Andoni Iraola, who similarly cites Bielsa as his reference.

These are coaches who, while taking the initiative, encourage vertical football. For as different as the clubs are, both the fans of United and Liverpool have enjoyed success when their teams have played high-octane football.

This summer's World Cup was a strong showcase of Pochettino's style of play and his recent tactical adaptation.

Rather than a fixed, positional style of play - akin to the work of somebody like Manchester City 's Enzo Maresca - Pochettino's USA had only certain players being tasked with holding their position.

This approach posed problems for teams who defended in a zonal manner - defending specific areas rather than individual players.

The US midfielders being able to move freely meant they could step into areas of the pitch between the zones that were being defended, which resulted in their players often being unmarked with time and space on the ball.

By playing in close proximity to each other in the middle of the pitch, the US found another benefit.

Small-space passing combinations helped draw the opposing team up towards the ball and combined with clever off-ball movement to stretch the pitch, allowed the US to find their striker with few defenders around him.

Pochettino's men looked to thread through-balls in behind and early after enticing the opposition's press and the speedy Folarin Balogun was able to turn those chances into goals.

Here is a good example of USA's fluid midfield four under Pochettino. The right-sided midfielder McKennie has placed himself near his three midfield team-mates, leaving the right half-space empty. With a four against three in that area of the pitch, USA are best placed to play quick combinations before looking to find their attackers in space.

Here we can see the swapping of left-winger Pulisic and left-back Robinson’s positions. In this example, Robinson inverts into the fluid midfield four with Pulisic positioned on the touchline for balance. When out wide, Pulisic was able to showcase impressive one-against-one dribbling throughout the match too.

This combination of a fluid midfield, small-space passing and direct through-balls doesn't sound dissimilar to what Carrick was trying to move towards implementing this season.

And although that may worry United fans, the similarity in principles will benefit the players.

"My philosophy is to give a freer style with a good organisation," were Pochettino's words in 2014.

Although philosophically similar, that latter part - a clearer organisation to his freer style - is likely to be what Carrick was unable to reliably offer his players.

For fans of top sides, fast-paced, vertical football tends to be accepted when it comes from a place of being proactive - think Ferguson's United or Jurgen Klopp's Liverpool - wanting to keep the ball, but not passing it for passing's sake.

Fast-paced, vertical football tends to be frowned upon when it comes from a place of conceding possession and defending your own goal for long periods of the match.

The first half of Carrick's stint did appear proactive, while his 4-2-4 press worked well. Leaving four players high was a risk that allowed them to win the ball back and score quickly, but as teams figured this out, United failed to adapt.

There also appeared to be a drop in the team's fitness the longer United went from the departure of ex-boss Ruben Amorim, who left United well conditioned, albeit on the back of a schedule without European football.

Here we see United's narrow 4-2-4 defensive shape in the first half against Como

Hiring Pochettino will immediately begin the process of turning United into a well-drilled side, capable of applying intense pressure, likely in a co-ordinated manner.

Pochettino enjoyed relative success with Spurs , built on this intensity and co-ordination, that differentiated him from the rest of the league.

With that unique selling point more common now than a decade ago, how he builds on it will dictate how his tenure unfolds.

But watching Brighton this season, he can be assured that an approach founded on intensity off the ball can work in the Premier League in 2026, with Fabian Hurzeler's men second in the league, with the fourth highest average possession, 10 games in.

Pochettino, from a footballing point of view, feels extremely aligned to the values of Ferguson's United, and as a result will implement numerous similarities to the things Carrick wanted, but ultimately failed, to deliver.

His wealth of experience make him a more proven entity than the departing United manager and if he can get his team fit and pressing high, in typically Pochettino fashion, they should see an upturn in form.

Expanding on his managerial approach, while managing Spurs he explained how "the most important thing [was] to create a good shape for players to be comfortable and to show their real qualities".

Rather than relying on pre-defined pattern, he looks to empower individuals to solve attacking problems. Taking this approach means recruitment of top talent matters more than ever.

"He [gave] me the confidence and licence to go where I wanted on the pitch, where I [could] use my strengths," said Cole Palmer, who enjoyed his most productive Premier League season under Pochettino at Chelsea .

United have good attackers but they will need to take the same initiative Palmer did, if platformed to their strengths - something Pochettino does well.

If they don't, and if Pochettino is to stumble, it will likely be in United's inability to break down stubborn defences when asked to dominate the ball - in what would feel like Groundhog Day, again.

Ambasaderi w’u Rwanda muri Mali ariko akagira icyicaro muri Senegal, Festus Bizimana, yasuye ikipe y’igihugu y’u Rwanda, Amavubi, n’umutoza wayo Stephen Constantine, mu Mujyi wa Bamako mbere y’umukino ugomba kuyihuza na Mali mu gushaka itike y'Igikombe cya Afurika 2027. Ambasaderi Bizimana yagaragarije abakinnyi n’abatoza ko bagomba kumenya ko bafite inkunga y’Abanyarwanda bose, anabagezaho ubutumwa bwo kubatera imbaraga bwaturutse ku Banyarwanda baba muri Mali, Senegal, Gambia, Guinea-Bissau na Cabo Verde.

Amavubi azahura na Mali, izwi nka Les Aigles, kuri uyu wa Gatanu tariki ya 13 Ugushyingo 2026, mu mukino wo gushaka itike y'Igikombe cya Afurika cya 2027 (AFCON 2027). Uyu mukino uteganyijwe kuba saa Moya ku isaha yo muri Mali bikaba saa 21h00 zo mu Rwanda ukabera kuri Stade du 26 Mars i Bamako.

Abanyarwanda benshi baba muri Mali na Senegal na bo biteganyijwe ko baza kwitabira uyu mukino, kugira ngo bashyigikire ikipe yabo kandi bayitere ingabo mu bitugu.

Abakinnyi b'ikipe y'Igihugu Amavubi, uretse ubutumwa bwo kubatera Ingabo mu bitugu bagejejweho na Ambasaderi Bizimana, ishyirahamwe ry'umupira w'amaguru mu Rwanda kandi ryabemereye ko agahimbazamusyi basanzwe bahabwa kakubwe kabiri kuri buri mukino usigaye aho basigaje imikino ine muri rusange.

Uyu mukino ni ingenzi ku Amavubi mu rugendo rwo gushaka itike y'iri rushanwa rikomeye ku mugabane wa Afurika dore ko u Rwanda rwaherukaga mu mikino ya nyuma y'Igikombe cya Afurika mu myaka 22 ishize.

MN202611_bl3s0uwoho.t:
FBI ivuga ko abazwiho gukora ubujura bifashishije ikoranabuhanga "hackers", bivugwa ko bakorera ubutegetsi bwa Koreya ya Ruguru bamaze kwiba arenga miliyoni 400 z'amadolari y'Amerika yo mu bwoko bwa 'cryptocurrency'.

Ibyo ngo babigeraho bakoresheje amashusho y'amahimbano kugira ngo bashuke abantu bibe amakuru yabo bwite, nk'uko inzego z'ubuyobozi za Leta Zunze Ubumwe za Amerika zibitangaza.

FBI igaragaza ko, mu mezi 18 ashize abantu barenga 900 bamaze kugwa muri ubu buriganya bwiswe "FaceStealer".

Umuyobozi wa FBI ushinzwe ibyaha bikorwa hifashishijwe ikoranabuhanga, Brett Leatherman, yagize ati: "Ubutegetsi bwa Koreya ya Ruguru bushingira ku mafaranga bukura mu bikorwa byo kwiba cryptocurrency kugira ngo butere inkunga gahunda yabwo yo gukora intwaro zitemewe".

Yunzemo ati: "mu myaka ishize, bwibye amamiliyari y'amadolari."

Ibi bibaye nyuma y'icyumweru kimwe Binance, urubuga runini ku isi ruvunjirizwaho amafaranga yo mu bwoko bw'ikoranabuhanga, azwi nka cryptocurrency, rutangaje ko abanyabyaha bakoresheje ibibazo by'akazi by'ibihimbano kugira ngo bibe agera kuri miliyari 6.3 z'amadolari.

Inzego zishinzwe umutekano muri Amerika zavuze ko igitero cyagabwe kuri Binance, gikekwa ko ari cyo gikomeye cyane cyo kwiba amafaranga yo mu ikoranabuhanga kugeza ubu.

Bemeza ko, cyaba cyarakozwe n'abanyabyaha bafitanye isano na Koreya ya Ruguru.

Amakuru ya BBC Gahuza ako kanya kuri WhatsApp yawe

Gusa ubutegetsi bwa Pyongyang bwahakanye ibyo bushinjwa.

Abayobozi bavuga ko uburiganya bwa FaceStealer ari bumwe mu buryo bushya abanyabyaha bakoresha, bwibanda cyane ku bantu bakora mu bijyanye na Cryptocurrency no mu ikoranabuhanga rya Web3, cyane cyane abakora mu guteza imbere no gufasha mu mikorere ya porogaramu za Open-source software.

Nk'uko FBI na Minisiteri y'Ubutabera ya Leta Zunze Ubumwe za Amerika bibivuga, aba banyabyaha bakoresha konti z'impimbano cyangwa izibwe ku mbuga nkoranyambaga kugira ngo batumire abantu mu nama zikorwa hakoreshejwe amashusho (video calls) kuri porogaramu z'impimbano zisa na Zoom, Microsoft Teams na Google Meet.

Nyuma yaho, berekana amashusho yafashwe mbere y'abantu bazi neza ko abo bashaka kuriganya bazi cyangwa bizeye, kugira ngo babumvishe ko barimo kugirana inama nyayo n'umuntu baziranye.

Ariko muri izo nama, amajwi aba asa n'afite ikibazo, ku buryo umuntu atayumva neza.

Hanyuma, kuri mudasobwa cyangwa telefoni y'uwatumiwe haza ubutumwa bumusaba gukemura icyo kibazo cy'amajwi akanda kuri link bamuha.

Iyo akanze kuri iyo link, virusi ihita yinjira mu gikoresho cye cy'ikoranabuhanga yakoreshaga.

Iyi virusi ituma abanyabyaha babasha kubona urutonde rw'abantu afitanye na bo imikoranire, ndetse na porogaramu akoresha, bityo bakabona abandi bantu bashobora kugerageza kuriganya.

Nk'uko inzego z'ubuyobozi za Amerika zibivuga, aba banyabyaha bafata amashusho y'izo nama mu ibanga, hanyuma bakayakoresha nk'ibikoresho byo kuriganya abandi bantu bashya.

FBI yavuze ko FaceStealer ari: "Uburyo bukomeye cyane bwo gushuka abantu binyuze mu mibanire yabo, kandi ko bushobora no kubeshya abantu bafite ubumenyi buhanitse mu ikoranabuhanga ndetse n'abazi neza iby'umutekano waryo."

Patrick Grandy, umuyobozi wungirije ushinzwe ishami rya FBI rikorera i Los Angeles, mu itangazo ryashyizwe ahagaragara ku wa kane, yagize ati: "Ubu buriganya bukoresha icyizere dufitiye porogaramu zisanzwe zikoreshwa mu nama ziba hifashishijwe ikoranabuhanga, ndetse n'icyizere tugirira abantu dufitanye na bo umubano mwiza."

Yakomeje agira ati:"Niba utekereza ko nta buryo na bumwe ushobora kugwa muri ubu buriganya, bivuze ko utanatekereje bihagije ku buryo bushobora gukoreshwa mu kukubeshya."

MN202611_b7bksnfq5h.t:
Perezida wa Repubulika y’u Rwanda, Paul Kagame, ari kumwe na Madamu Jeannette Kagame, bakiriwe ku mugaragaro n’Umwami wa Cambodia, Norodom Sihamoni, mu muhango wo kubakira ku rwego rw’Igihugu wabereye mu Ngoro y’Umwami iri mu murwa mukuru Phnom Penh.

Uyu muhango wabaye mu gitondo cyo kuri uyu wa 13 Ugushyingo 2026, mu gihe Perezida Kagame na Madamu Jeannette Kagame batangiye uruzinduko rw’akazi mu Bwami bwa Cambodia.

Nyuma y’umuhango wo kubakira ku rwego rw’Igihugu, Umwami Norodom Sihamoni yagiranye ikiganiro cyihariye na Perezida Kagame, mu muhango uzwi nka Royal Audience, aho Umukuru w’Igihugu cy’u Rwanda yakiriwe n’Umwami mu rwego rw’imikoranire isanzwe iherekeza ingendo z’akazi z’abakuru b’ibihugu.

Uru ruzinduko rwa Perezida Kagame muri Cambodia rugamije gukomeza umubano n’imikoranire hagati y’u Rwanda n’iki gihugu cyo mu Majyepfo ashyira Uburasirazuba bwa Aziya.

Ni uruzinduko rwitezweho gukomeza guha imbaraga umubano w’ibihugu byombi, binyuze mu biganiro n’ubufatanye mu nzego zinyuranye.

Cambodia ni igihugu giherereye mu Majyepfo ashyira Uburasirazuba bwa Aziya, kizwi cyane kubera amateka akomeye, arimo ingoro z'amateka, ubukerarugendo, umuco gakondo n'ubwami bumaze ibinyejana byinshi.

Kuba Perezida Paul Kagame ari muri iki gihugu mu ruzinduko rw’akazi ni umwanya mwiza wo kumenya amateka yacyo, imiyoborere, ubukungu n'amahirwe y'ubufatanye gishobora kugirana n'u Rwanda.

Cambodia ifite amateka akomeye cyane ajyanye n'Ubwami bwa Khmer bwabayeho hagati y'ikinyejana cya cyenda n'icya cumi na gatanu.

Ubwami bwa Khmer bwagize uruhare rukomeye mu mateka ya Aziya y'Amajyepfo ashyira Uburasirazuba, haba mu buhanzi, imyubakire, ubuhinzi n'imiyoborere.

Ikimenyetso gikomeye cy'ayo mateka ni Angkor Wat, imwe mu ngoro z'amateka zizwi cyane ku Isi, yubatswe mu kinyejana cya 12.

Cambodia yananyuze mu bihe bikomeye by'amateka, cyane cyane mu gihe cy'ubutegetsi bwa Khmer Rouge hagati ya 1975 na 1979, ubwo igihugu cyanyuraga mu bwicanyi ndengakamere, inzara n'ihonyorwa ry'uburenganzira bwa muntu.

Ibyo bihe byasize amateka akomeye mu mibereho y'Abanyakambodiya.

Cambodia ni ubwami bugendera ku Itegeko Nshinga (Constitutional Monarchy).

Umwami wayo ni Norodom Sihamoni, wasimbuye se Norodom Sihanouk mu mwaka wa 2004.

Umwami ni ikimenyetso cy'ubumwe n'ubusugire bw'igihugu, ariko imiyoborere ya buri munsi ishingiye kuri Guverinoma iyobowe na Minisitiri w'Intebe.

Inteko Ishinga Amategeko igizwe n'imitwe ibiri: National Assembly. Senate.

Banki y'Isi igaragaza ko ubukungu bwa Cambodia bwazamutse ku kigero cya 8.2% ku mwaka mu mpuzandengo hagati ya 2000 na 2019. Mu 2024 bwazamutseho 6%, mu gihe ishoramari rituruka mu mahanga ryakomeje kugira uruhare rukomeye mu iterambere ry'inganda.

Mu Ugushyingo 2025, ibihugu byombi byasinyanye amasezerano ajyanye no kugirana ibiganiro bya dipolomasi hagati ya Minisiteri z'Ububanyi n'Amahanga ndetse no korohereza abafite pasiporo za dipolomasi n'iz'akazi mu bijyanye na viza.

Muri Mata 2023, Banki Nkuru y'u Rwanda (BNR) na Banki Nkuru ya Cambodia byasinyanye amasezerano y'ubufatanye mu iterambere ry'urwego rw'imari.

Naho muri Gicurasi uyu mwaka, izo banki zatangaje ubufatanye mu koroshya uburyo bwo kwishyurana hakoreshejwe ikoranabuhanga hagati y'ibihugu byombi.
